<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_SOLVERS -->
  <Solvers>

    <CompositionalMultiphaseFVM
      name="compflow"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="fluidTPFA"
      targetRegions="{ reservoir }"      
      temperature="300"
      useMass="1"
      initialDt="1e3"
      maxCompFractionChange="0.1">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-4"
        newtonMaxIter="40"
        maxTimeStepCuts="10"
        lineSearchAction="None"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        solverType="fgmres"
        preconditionerType="mgr"
        krylovTol="1.0e-5"/>
    </CompositionalMultiphaseFVM>

  </Solvers>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_SOLVERS_END -->  

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_EVENTS -->
  <Events
    maxTime="2e6">

   <PeriodicEvent
      name="outputs"
      timeFrequency="5e5"
      targetExactTimestep="1"
      target="/Outputs/vtkOutput"/>
    
    <PeriodicEvent
      name="solverApplications"
      maxEventDt="5e5"
      target="/Solvers/compflow"/>

    <PeriodicEvent name="sourceFluxStatsEvent"
      timeFrequency="5e5"
      target="/Tasks/fluxesStats" />

    <PeriodicEvent
      name="restarts"
      timeFrequency="1e6"
      targetExactTimestep="0"
      target="/Outputs/restartOutput"/>

  </Events>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_EVENTS_END -->  


  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_NUMERICAL_METHODS -->  
  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteVolume>
      <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="fluidTPFA"/>
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_NUMERICAL_METHODS_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_ELEMENT_REGIONS -->
  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="reservoir"
      cellBlocks="{ * }"
      materialList="{ fluid, rock, relperm }"/>
  </ElementRegions>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_ELEMENT_REGIONS_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_CONSTITUTIVE -->
  <Constitutive>

    <DeadOilFluid
      name="fluid"
      phaseNames="{ oil, water }"
      surfaceDensities="{ 800.0, 1022.0 }"
      componentMolarWeight="{ 114e-3, 18e-3 }"
      hydrocarbonFormationVolFactorTableNames="{ B_o_table }"
      hydrocarbonViscosityTableNames="{ visc_o_table }"
      waterReferencePressure="30600000.1"
      waterFormationVolumeFactor="1.03"
      waterCompressibility="0.00000000041"
      waterViscosity="0.0003"/>

    <CompressibleSolidConstantPermeability
      name="rock"
      solidModelName="nullSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"/>

    <NullModel
      name="nullSolid"/>

    <PressurePorosity
      name="rockPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="0.1"
      referencePressure="1.0e7"
      compressibility="1e-10"/>

    <BrooksCoreyRelativePermeability
      name="relperm"
      phaseNames="{ oil, water }"
      phaseMinVolumeFraction="{ 0.0, 0.0 }"
      phaseRelPermExponent="{ 2.0, 2.0 }"
      phaseRelPermMaxValue="{ 1.0, 1.0 }"/>

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="rockPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-14, 1.0e-14, 1.0e-18 }"/>
    
  </Constitutive>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_CONSTITUTIVE_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_FIELD_SPECS -->  
  <FieldSpecifications>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="permx"
      component="0"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="rockPerm_permeability"
      functionName="permxFunc"
      scale="9.869233e-16"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="permy"
      component="1"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="rockPerm_permeability"
      functionName="permyFunc"
      scale="9.869233e-16"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="permz"
      component="2"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="rockPerm_permeability"
      functionName="permzFunc"
      scale="9.869233e-16"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="referencePorosity"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="rockPorosity_referencePorosity"
      functionName="poroFunc"
      scale="1.0"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialPressure"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="4.1369e+7"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialComposition_oil"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="globalCompFraction"
      component="0"
      scale="0.9995"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialComposition_water"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="globalCompFraction"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0005"/>
    
    <SourceFlux
      name="sourceTerm"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      scale="-0.07279"
      component="1"
      setNames="{ source }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkPressure"
      setNames="{ sink1, sink2, sink3, sink4 }"         
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="2.7579e+7"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkComposition_oil"
      setNames="{ sink1, sink2, sink3, sink4 }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="globalCompFraction"
      component="0"
      scale="0.9995"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkComposition_water"
      setNames="{ sink1, sink2, sink3, sink4 }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/reservoir/block"
      fieldName="globalCompFraction"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0005"/>

  </FieldSpecifications>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_FIELD_SPECS_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_FUNCTIONS -->  
  <Functions>
    <TableFunction 
      name="permxFunc"
      inputVarNames="{elementCenter}"
      coordinateFiles="{xlin.geos,ylin.geos,zlin.geos}"
      voxelFile="permx.geos"
      interpolation="linear" />
    <TableFunction 
      name="permyFunc"
      inputVarNames="{elementCenter}"
      coordinateFiles="{xlin.geos,ylin.geos,zlin.geos}"
      voxelFile="permy.geos"
      interpolation="linear" />
    <TableFunction 
      name="permzFunc"
      inputVarNames="{elementCenter}"
      coordinateFiles="{xlin.geos,ylin.geos,zlin.geos}"
      voxelFile="permz.geos"
      interpolation="linear" />
    <TableFunction 
      name="poroFunc"
      inputVarNames="{elementCenter}"
      coordinateFiles="{xlin.geos,ylin.geos,zlin.geos}"
      voxelFile="poro.geos"
      interpolation="linear" />

    <TableFunction
      name="B_o_table"
      coordinateFiles="{ pres_pvdo.txt }"
      voxelFile="B_o_pvdo.txt"
      interpolation="linear"/>

    <TableFunction
      name="visc_o_table"
      coordinateFiles="{ pres_pvdo.txt }"
      voxelFile="visc_pvdo.txt"
      interpolation="linear"/>
    
  </Functions>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_FUNCTIONS_END -->    

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_TASKS -->    
  <Tasks>
    <SourceFluxStatistics name="fluxesStats"
      flowSolverName="compflow"
      fluxNames="{*}"
      logLevel="2"
      writeCSV="1" />
  </Tasks>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_TASKS_END -->      

  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_OUTPUTS -->    
  <Outputs>
    <VTK
      name="vtkOutput"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
    
  </Outputs>
  <!-- SPHINX_TUT_DEAD_OIL_BOTTOM_SPE10_OUTPUTS_END -->      
  
</Problem>

title: .. _ExampleVerticalPoroElastoPlasticWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Vertical PoroElasto-Plastic Wellbore Simulation

## Overview and Simulation Type

This specification describes a coupled poromechanical simulation of a vertical wellbore problem in porous media. The simulation models rock deformation near a wellbore considering elastoplastic deformation, fluid diffusion, and poromechanical coupling effects. Two variants of this simulation exist: a poroelastic version for verification purposes and a poroplastic version that captures plastic deformation behavior. The problem involves a vertical wellbore subjected to anisotropic stress conditions with mechanical and fluid loading applied at the wellbore wall.

## Solver Configuration

The simulation requires three solver definitions that work together:

### Primary Mechanics Solver
Create a solid mechanics solver of type "SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM" with the name "mechanicsSolver". This solver handles the mechanical deformation using a Lagrangian finite element method.

### Flow Solver
Create a single-phase flow solver of type "SinglePhaseFVM" with the name "SinglePhaseFlowSolver". This solver handles fluid flow using the finite volume method.

### Coupling Solver
Create a coupling solver of type "SinglePhasePoromechanics" with the name "PoromechanicsSolver". This solver must reference the fluid solver "SinglePhaseFlowSolver" and the solid solver "mechanicsSolver". The porous material name should be set to "porousRock". The discretization method should reference "FE1" and the target region should be "Omega".

## Mesh Configuration

Use the internal wellbore mesh generator "InternalWellbore" to create the computational domain with the following specifications:

- **Domain dimensions**: 10 meters by 5 meters by 2 meters
- **Wellbore radius**: 0.1 meters (initial radius)
- **Wellbore trajectory**: Define trajectory coordinates that represent a perfect vertical well
- **Automatic radial element spacing**: Enable using autoSpaceRadialElems set to "{ 1 }", which automatically determines the number and spacing of elements in the radial direction
- **Outer boundary type**: Set useCartesianOuterBoundary to "0" to enforce a Cartesian-aligned outer boundary on the outer block
- **Element counts**: The mesh should contain 100 elements in the radial direction, 80 elements in the tangential direction, and 2 elements in the z-direction
- **Element type**: Eight-node hexahedral elements (C3D8)
- **Cell block name**: Name the cell block "cb1"

The mesh generator will create refinement that conforms to the wellbore geometry.

## Numerical Methods

### Finite Element Discretization
Define a finite element discretization method named "FE1" using linear basis functions and Gaussian quadrature rules. This method is used by both the coupling solver and the solid mechanics solver.

### Finite Volume Discretization
Define a two-point flux approximation scheme named "singlePhaseTPFA" for the flow discretization.

## Constitutive Models and Material Properties

### For Poroelastic Case

**Solid Material (rock)**:
Use the "PorousElasticIsotropic" model with the following properties:
- Bulk Modulus: 11.11 GPa
- Shear Modulus: 8.33 GPa

**Fluid Material (water)**:
Use the "CompressibleSinglePhaseFluid" model with:
- Density: 1000.0 kg/m³
- Viscosity: 0.001 Pa·s
- Compressibility: 2.09 × 10⁻¹⁰ Pa⁻¹

### For Poroplastic Case

**Solid Material (rock)**:
Use the "PorousExtendedDruckerPrager" model with:
- Bulk Modulus: 11.11 GPa
- Shear Modulus: 8.33 GPa
- Default Cohesion: 1.0 MPa
- Default Initial Friction Angle: 15.27 degrees
- Default Residual Friction Angle: 23.05 degrees
- Default Hardening Rate: 0.01 (since residual friction angle is larger than initial, strain hardening is automatically selected)
- Default Dilation Ratio: 1.0 (corresponds to an associated flow rule)

**Fluid Material (water)**:
Use the "CompressibleSinglePhaseFluid" model with identical properties as the poroelastic case.

### Porosity and Permeability Models

**Porosity Model (rockPorosity)**:
Define a stress-dependent porosity model with:
- Reference porosity: 0.3

**Permeability Model (rockPerm)**:
Define a constant permeability model with:
- Permeability: 1.0 × 10⁻²⁰ m²

## Initial Conditions

All initial condition fields must have the initialCondition attribute set to "1".

### Initial Stress State
Apply anisotropic in-situ stresses:
- Minimum horizontal stress (σh): -9.0 MPa (compression is negative)
- Maximum horizontal stress (σH): -11.0 MPa
- Vertical stress (σv): -12.0 MPa

### Initial Pore Pressure
Initialize the pore pressure field throughout the domain as required for the coupled simulation.

## Boundary Conditions

### Wellbore Wall Conditions (applied to surface "rneg")

**Mechanical Loading (InnerMechanicalLoad)**:
- Apply a normal traction with tractionType set to "normal"
- Scale value: -10.0e6 (representing -10 MPa compressive traction)
- The traction is computed as the product of the scale value and the outward face normal
- Use a table function named "timeFunction" to define time-dependent loading

**Fluid Loading (InnerFluidLoad)**:
- Apply fluid pressure of 10.0 MPa at the wellbore wall
- Use the same time function for time-dependent behavior

### Outer Boundary Conditions

Apply roller constraints to all outer boundary surfaces. Use the shorthand notations:
- "xneg" for the left-most boundary in x-direction
- "xpos" for the right-most boundary in x-direction  
- "yneg" for the left-most boundary in y-direction
- "ypos" for the right-most boundary in y-direction
- "zpos" for the top boundary in z-direction
- "zneg" for the bottom boundary in z-direction

The boundary conditions should constrain normal displacement while allowing tangential movement (roller conditions).

### Time Function Definition

Create a table function named "timeFunction" that defines coordinates (time values) and corresponding values (magnitude multipliers) to specify the time history of the loading. This function controls how the wellbore wall loads are applied over the simulation duration.

## Field Specifications Notes

When specifying field conditions:
- Use "nodeManager" in the objectPath for boundary conditions applied to element nodes
- Use "faceManager" in the objectPath for boundary conditions applied to element faces
- Use component indices 0, 1, and 2 to refer to x, y, and z directions respectively
- The fieldName attribute must match the registered field names in GEOS
- The setName attribute should reference previously defined geometric sets or shorthand boundaries

## Output Configuration

### Simulation Duration
Configure the Events section to run the simulation for 497,640 seconds. This corresponds to a non-dimensional end time of t* = 4.62 when using the analytical solution scaling.

### Output Format
Request silo-format output files for visualization in tools such as VisIt.

### Output Variables
The simulation should output fields including:
- Pore pressure distribution
- Radial displacement
- Effective radial stress
- Effective tangential stress
- For the poroplastic case: stress components (particularly σyy) to observe stress relaxation due to plasticity

## Region Definition

Define a single computational region named "Omega" that encompasses the entire rock domain. Both the coupling solver and individual physics solvers should target this region. Associate the porous material "porousRock" with this region, linking together all the constitutive models (solid, fluid, porosity, permeability).
xml_content:
<Problem>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_TABLE -->
<Functions>
  <TableFunction 
    name="timeFunction"
    inputVarNames="{time}"
    coordinates="{0.0, 0.1, 1e6}"
    values="{0.0, 1.0, 1.0}" 
  />
</Functions>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_TABLE_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_MATERIAL -->
<Constitutive>
  <PorousElasticIsotropic
    name="porousRock"
    solidModelName="rock"
    porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
    permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
  />
  <ElasticIsotropic
    name="rock"
    defaultDensity="2700"
    defaultBulkModulus="1.1111e10"
    defaultShearModulus="8.3333e9"
  />
  <CompressibleSinglePhaseFluid 
    name="water"
    defaultDensity="1000"
    defaultViscosity="0.001"
    referencePressure="0e6"
    referenceDensity="1000"
    compressibility="2.09028227021e-10"
    referenceViscosity="0.001"
    viscosibility="0.0"
  />
  <BiotPorosity
    name="rockPorosity"
    defaultGrainBulkModulus="1.0e27"
    defaultReferencePorosity="0.3"
  />    
  <ConstantPermeability
    name="rockPerm"
    permeabilityComponents="{1.0e-20, 1.0e-20, 1.0e-20}"
  /> 
</Constitutive>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_MATERIAL_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_ELEMENTREGIONS -->
<ElementRegions>
  <CellElementRegion 
    name="Omega" 
    cellBlocks="{ * }" 
    materialList="{ water, porousRock }"
  />
</ElementRegions>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_ELEMENTREGIONS_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_BC -->
<FieldSpecifications>
  <FieldSpecification 
    name="stressXX"
    initialCondition="1"
    setNames="{all}"
    objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
    fieldName="rock_stress"
    component="0"
    scale="-9.0e6"
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="stressYY"
    initialCondition="1"
    setNames="{all}"
    objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
    fieldName="rock_stress"
    component="1"
    scale="-11.0e6"
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="stressZZ"
    initialCondition="1"
    setNames="{all}"
    objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
    fieldName="rock_stress"
    component="2"
    scale="-12.0e6"
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="initialPressure"
    initialCondition="1"
    setNames="{all}"
    objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
    fieldName="pressure"
    scale="0e6"
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="xconstraint"    
    objectPath="nodeManager" 
    fieldName="totalDisplacement" 
    component="0" 
    scale="0.0" 
    setNames="{xneg, xpos}"
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="yconstraint"    
    objectPath="nodeManager" 
    fieldName="totalDisplacement" 
    component="1" 
    scale="0.0" 
    setNames="{tneg, tpos, ypos}"
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="zconstraint" 
    objectPath="nodeManager" 
    fieldName="totalDisplacement" 
    component="2" 
    scale="0.0" 
    setNames="{zneg, zpos}"
  />

  <Traction 
    name="InnerMechanicalLoad"
    setNames="{ rneg }"
    objectPath="faceManager"
    scale="-10.0e6"
    tractionType="normal"
    functionName="timeFunction"     
  />

  <FieldSpecification 
    name="InnerFluidLoad"
    setNames="{ rneg }"
    objectPath="faceManager"
    fieldName="pressure"
    scale="10e6"
    functionName="timeFunction"   
  />
</FieldSpecifications>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_BC_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_POROMECHANICSSOLVER -->
<Solvers gravityVector="{0.0, 0.0, 0.0}">
<SinglePhasePoromechanics 
  name="PoromechanicsSolver" 
  solidSolverName="mechanicsSolver"
  flowSolverName="SinglePhaseFlowSolver"
  logLevel="1"
  targetRegions="{Omega}">
  <LinearSolverParameters 
    solverType="direct"
    directParallel="0"
    logLevel="0"
  />
  <NonlinearSolverParameters
    newtonMaxIter = "40"
  />
</SinglePhasePoromechanics>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_POROMECHANICSSOLVER_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_MECHANICALSOLVER -->
<SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM 
  name="mechanicsSolver" 
  logLevel="1"
  discretization="FE1"
  targetRegions="{ Omega }"
  >
  <NonlinearSolverParameters
    newtonTol = "1.0e-5"
    newtonMaxIter = "15"
  />  
</SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_MECHANICALSOLVER_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_SINGLEPHASEFVM -->
<SinglePhaseFVM 
  name="SinglePhaseFlowSolver"
  logLevel="1"
  discretization="singlePhaseTPFA"
  targetRegions="{Omega}"> 
  <NonlinearSolverParameters
    newtonTol = "1.0e-6"
    newtonMaxIter = "8"
  /> 
</SinglePhaseFVM>
</Solvers>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_SINGLEPHASEFVM_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_NUMERICAL -->
<NumericalMethods>
  <FiniteElements>
    <FiniteElementSpace 
      name="FE1"
      order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>
  <FiniteVolume>
    <TwoPointFluxApproximation 
      name="singlePhaseTPFA"
    />
  </FiniteVolume>
</NumericalMethods>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_NUMERICAL_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_OUTPUT -->
<Outputs>
  <Silo 
    name="siloOutput"
    parallelThreads="1"
    plotFileRoot="plot"
  />

  <Restart
    name="restartOutput"
  />  
</Outputs>
<!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_OUTPUT_END -->

</Problem>

natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Cased Thermoelastic Wellbore Simulation

## Overview and Simulation Type

Create an XML configuration file for a cased thermoelastic wellbore simulation using GEOS. This simulation models a wellbore system consisting of three concentric cylindrical layers: a steel casing (innermost), a cement sheath (middle), and the surrounding rock formation (outermost). The problem involves thermal loading where a uniform temperature change is applied to the inner surface of the casing.

The solver type should be **SinglePhasePoromechanics** with the thermal option enabled. This couples thermal diffusion with mechanical deformation. The simulation assumes isotropic linear thermoelastic behavior for all three materials. No separation or thermal barrier is permitted at the casing-cement and cement-rock contact interfaces. The problem is solved under plane strain conditions, meaning only radial thermal diffusion on a single horizontal layer is considered.

## Mesh Requirements

Use the **InternalWellbore** internal mesh generator to create the computational domain. Configure the mesh with the following specifications:

1. **Radial geometry**: Define a vector of radii that specifies the boundaries of each cylindrical region - the inner casing radius, the outer casing radius (which equals the inner cement radius), the outer cement radius (which equals the inner rock formation radius), and the far-field outer boundary of the rock formation.

2. **Angular extent**: Set the theta angle range from 0 to 90 degrees to simulate a quarter of the wellbore geometry, taking advantage of axisymmetric conditions.

3. **Vertical trajectory**: Define a vertical well trajectory since only a single horizontal plane is being modeled under plane strain conditions.

4. **Element sizing**: Enable the autoSpaceRadialElems parameter to automatically optimize element sizes, increasing them progressively from the wellbore toward the far-field zone. Apply this automatic spacing specifically to the rock formation layer only.

5. **Outer boundary shape**: Set useCartesianOuterBoundary to a value of 3 for the rock layer, which transforms the far-field boundary into a circular shape.

6. **Region definitions**: Define cellBlockNames to identify the three distinct regions (casing, cement sheath, and rock formation) with their associated element types specified in elementTypes.

## Material Properties and Constitutive Models

### Thermoelastic Solid Properties

For each of the three materials (casing, cement, rock), define the following properties within the Constitutive section:

1. **Elastic moduli**: Specify the drained bulk modulus and shear modulus for each material.

2. **Thermal expansion**: Define the drained linear thermal expansion coefficient that relates stress change to temperature change.

3. **Solid density**: Include solid density values for each material, though these will not affect results since gravitational effects are ignored in this simulation.

### Poroelastic Properties

Configure porosity and Biot coefficient settings to effectively simulate pure thermoelastic coupling without fluid flow effects:

1. **Porosity**: Set a negligible (near-zero) porosity value for all three materials.

2. **Biot coefficient**: Enforce a zero Biot coefficient by setting the elastic bulk modulus of the solid skeleton (Ks) equal to the drained bulk modulus (K), since the Biot coefficient is calculated as b = 1 - K/Ks.

### Thermal Properties

Define thermal transport properties for all three layers:

1. **Thermal conductivity**: Specify conductivity values for casing, cement, and rock materials.

2. **Volumetric heat capacity**: Define the solid volumetric heat capacity for each of the three materials.

### Permeability Properties

Assign ultra-low permeability values to all three layers (casing, cement, and rock) to effectively eliminate fluid flow and simulate a pure thermoelastic problem.

### Fluid Properties

Configure fluid properties to eliminate thermal convection effects:

1. **Volumetric heat capacity**: Set a negligible volumetric heat capacity for the fluid to ensure that thermal transfer occurs only through diffusion, not convection.

2. **Other fluid properties**: While viscosity and thermal expansion coefficient must be defined, their values are not critical since fluid flow is ignored and pore pressure remains zero throughout the simulation.

## Initial Conditions

### Initial Temperature

Establish an initial reservoir temperature that serves as the reference temperature throughout the domain and at the far-field boundary.

### Initial Stress State

Configure initial effective stress for each layer (casing, cement, and rock) that is consistent with the initial temperature. The initial effective principal stress must be calculated according to the relationship: σ₀ = 3Kα·δT₀, where σ₀ is the initial effective principal stress, δT₀ is the initial temperature change from a reference state, K is the drained bulk modulus, and α is the drained linear thermal expansion coefficient of each respective material.

### Initial Pore Pressure

Set zero pore pressure throughout the entire domain to maintain the assumption of a thermoelastic problem without fluid flow consideration.

## Boundary Conditions

### Mechanical Boundary Conditions

1. **Axisymmetric plane strain constraints**: Apply displacement boundary conditions on the appropriate surfaces to enforce axisymmetric plane strain conditions. This includes constraining normal displacements on the symmetry planes at theta equals 0 degrees and theta equals 90 degrees.

2. **Far-field boundary fixity**: Constrain the far-field outer boundary to have zero displacement in all directions, based on the assumption that local changes near the wellbore have negligible effect on the distant boundary.

3. **Inner casing surface traction**: Apply a traction-free (zero traction) boundary condition on the inner surface of the casing.

### Thermal Boundary Conditions

1. **Inner surface temperature**: Apply a specified temperature corresponding to a cold fluid on the inner surface of the casing. This temperature should be lower than the initial reservoir temperature to create the thermal loading.

2. **Far-field temperature**: Maintain the initial reservoir temperature at the far-field boundary.

### Hydraulic Boundary Conditions

Enforce zero pore pressure conditions throughout the domain to ensure no fluid flow occurs during the simulation.

## Solver Configuration

Configure the SinglePhasePoromechanics solver with thermal coupling enabled. The solver should handle the coupled thermal diffusion and mechanical deformation problem. Since this is a validation study comparing against analytical solutions obtained using an implicit 1D finite difference method, ensure appropriate numerical parameters are selected for accuracy.

## Output Requirements

### Data Format

Configure output in HDF5 format to facilitate post-processing with Python scripts.

### Field Data Collection

Set up data collection for the following fields across all time steps:

1. **Temperature field**: Collect temperature data from all three layers (casing, cement, and rock formation).

2. **Solid stress field**: Collect stress tensor components from all three material regions, particularly the radial and hoop (tangential) stress components for validation purposes.

3. **Displacement field**: Collect displacement data for the entire domain using the nodeManager, which captures nodal displacement values.

### Time History Output

Configure time history outputs for:
- Temperature evolution
- Stress evolution  
- Displacement evolution

### Periodic Events

Define periodic events to trigger the collection of field data at specified intervals throughout the simulation. This includes separate periodic events for displacement field collection and other output quantities. The events should capture data at time points suitable for comparison against the reference analytical solution.

## File Organization

The configuration should be organized potentially across multiple XML files:
- A base XML file containing the core material properties, boundary conditions, and output definitions
- A benchmark-specific XML file containing mesh parameters and any case-specific settings
- The benchmark file should include the InternalWellbore mesh generator configuration with the specific geometric parameters
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <Solvers>
    <SinglePhasePoromechanics
      name="thermoElasticSolver"
      solidSolverName="solidMechSolver"
      flowSolverName="flowSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock }">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        couplingType="FullyImplicit"
        maxAllowedResidualNorm="1e19"
        newtonMaxIter="100"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"/>
    </SinglePhasePoromechanics>

    <SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM
      name="solidMechSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="FE1"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock }">
    </SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM>
   
    <SinglePhaseFVM
      name="flowSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="tpfaFlow"
      temperature="0"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock }">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
	normType="L2"/>
    </SinglePhaseFVM>
  </Solvers>

  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>

    <FiniteVolume>
      <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="tpfaFlow"/>
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="casing"
      cellBlocks="{ casing }"
      materialList="{ fluid, casing, casingThermalCond }"/>

    <CellElementRegion
      name="cement"
      cellBlocks="{ cement }"
      materialList="{ fluid, cement, cementThermalCond }"/>

    <CellElementRegion
      name="rock"
      cellBlocks="{ rock }"
      materialList="{ fluid, rock, rockThermalCond }"/>
  </ElementRegions>

  <Constitutive>

    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="casing"
      solidModelName="casingSolid"
      porosityModelName="casingPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="casingPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="casingInternalEnergy"/>

    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="cement"
      solidModelName="cementSolid"
      porosityModelName="cementPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="cementPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="cementInternalEnergy"/>

    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="rock"
      solidModelName="rockSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_PoroElasticProperties -->
    <BiotPorosity
      name="casingPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1e-6"
      defaultGrainBulkModulus="159.4202899e9"/>

    <BiotPorosity
      name="cementPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1e-6"
      defaultGrainBulkModulus="2.298850575e9"/>

    <BiotPorosity
      name="rockPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1e-6"
      defaultGrainBulkModulus="5.535714286e9"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_PoroElasticPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_HeatCapacityProperties -->
    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="casingInternalEnergy"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="1.375e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>

    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="cementInternalEnergy"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="4.2e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>

    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="rockInternalEnergy"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="4.56e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_HeatCapacityPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_PermeabilityProperties -->
    <ConstantPermeability
      name="casingPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100 }"/>

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="cementPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100 }"/>

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="rockPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100 }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_PermeabilityPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_ThermalProperties -->
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="casingThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 15, 15, 15 }"/>

    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="cementThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 }"/>

    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="rockThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.66, 1.66, 1.66 }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ThermalPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_FluidProperties -->
    <ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid
      name="fluid"
      defaultDensity="1000"
      defaultViscosity="1e-3"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      referenceTemperature="20.0"
      compressibility="5e-10"
      thermalExpansionCoeff="1e-10"
      viscosibility="0.0"
      specificHeatCapacity="1"
      referenceInternalEnergy="1"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_FluidPropertiesEnd -->

	<!-- SPHINX_ThermoElasticProperties -->
    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="casingSolid"
      defaultDensity="7500"
      defaultBulkModulus="159.4202899e9"
      defaultShearModulus="86.61417323e9"
      defaultDrainedLinearTEC="1.2e-5"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="cementSolid"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="2.298850575e9"
      defaultShearModulus="1.652892562e9"
      defaultDrainedLinearTEC="2.0e-5"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="rockSolid"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="5.535714286e9"
      defaultShearModulus="3.81147541e9"
      defaultDrainedLinearTEC="2.0e-5"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ThermoElasticPropertiesEnd -->
    
  </Constitutive>

  <FieldSpecifications>

    <!-- SPHINX_FixedFarFieldBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="rPosConstraint_x"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ rpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="rPosConstraint_y"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ rpos }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_FixedFarFieldBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_PlaneStrainAxisymmetryBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="tNegConstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tneg }"/>

   <FieldSpecification
      name="tPosConstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="zconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ zneg, zpos }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_PlaneStrainAxisymmetryBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_StressCasingInit -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_x_casing"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_y_casing"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_z_casing"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_StressCasingInitEnd -->

    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_x_cement"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_y_cement"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_z_cement"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_x_rock"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_y_rock"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_z_rock"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroPorePressureBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="zeroPressure"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sourcePressure"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkPressure"
      setNames="{ rpos }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroPorePressureBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialTemperature"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="farfieldTemperature"
      setNames="{ rpos }"       
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="innerTemperature"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="-20.0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroInnerTractionBC -->
    <Traction
      name="innerPressure"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      tractionType="normal"
      scale="0.0e6"
      setNames="{ rneg }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroInnerTractionBCEnd -->

  </FieldSpecifications>

  <Tasks>

    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="temperatureCollection_casing"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="temperature"/>
    <PackCollection
      name="temperatureCollection_cement"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="temperature"/>
    <PackCollection
      name="temperatureCollection_rock"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="temperature"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureCollectionEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="stressCollection_casing"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"/>
    <PackCollection
      name="stressCollection_cement"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"/>
    <PackCollection
      name="stressCollection_rock"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressCollectionEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="displacementCollection"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollectionEnd -->

  </Tasks>

  <Outputs>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="temperatureHistoryOutput_casing"
      sources="{ /Tasks/temperatureCollection_casing }"
      filename="temperatureHistory_casing"/>
    <TimeHistory
      name="temperatureHistoryOutput_cement"
      sources="{ /Tasks/temperatureCollection_cement }"
      filename="temperatureHistory_cement"/>
    <TimeHistory
      name="temperatureHistoryOutput_rock"
      sources="{ /Tasks/temperatureCollection_rock }"
      filename="temperatureHistory_rock"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="stressHistoryOutput_casing"
      sources="{ /Tasks/stressCollection_casing }"
      filename="stressHistory_casing"/>
    <TimeHistory
      name="stressHistoryOutput_cement"
      sources="{ /Tasks/stressCollection_cement }"
      filename="stressHistory_cement"/>
    <TimeHistory
      name="stressHistoryOutput_rock"
      sources="{ /Tasks/stressCollection_rock }"
      filename="stressHistory_rock"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="displacementHistoryOutput"
      sources="{ /Tasks/displacementCollection }"
      filename="displacementHistory"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <VTK
      name="vtkOutput"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>
</Problem>

title: .. _AdvancedExampleCasedElasticWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Cased Elastic Wellbore Simulation

## Overview and Simulation Type

This specification describes a solid mechanics simulation for a cased wellbore subjected to a pressure test. The model represents a completed wellbore consisting of three concentric cylindrical regions: an inner steel casing, a cement sheath surrounding the casing, and the outer rock formation. The simulation assumes isotropic linear elastic behavior for all three materials and enforces perfect bonding (no separation) at the casing-cement and cement-rock contact interfaces.

## Solver Configuration

### Primary Solver
Configure a Lagrangian finite element solid mechanics solver using the solver type "SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM". This problem does not involve fluid flow, so only the mechanical solver is needed.

### Target Regions and Materials
The solver must be configured to target three distinct regions corresponding to:
1. The steel casing region
2. The cement sheath region
3. The rock formation region

Each region must be associated with its corresponding solid material through the solver's material assignment parameters.

## Mesh Specification

### Mesh Generator Type
Use the internal wellbore mesh generator ("InternalWellbore") to create the computational domain.

### Geometric Parameters
- **Radii**: Define a vector of radii that specifies the boundaries of each cylindrical region - the inner radius of the casing, the outer radius of the casing (inner radius of cement), the outer radius of the cement sheath (inner radius of rock), and the far-field boundary of the rock formation.
- **Angular extent**: Specify the theta angle from 0 to 360 degrees for a full circumferential geometry. Note that reduced domains can be modeled using 0 to 180 degrees for half geometry or 0 to 90 degrees for quarter geometry.
- **Well trajectory**: Define a vertical well trajectory.

### Mesh Control Options
- **Automatic radial element spacing**: Enable the auto-spacing option for radial elements, which optimally increases element size from the near-wellbore zone to the far-field zone. Apply this automatic spacing specifically to the rock formation region.
- **Cartesian outer boundary**: Enable the option to transform the far-field boundary into a squared (Cartesian-aligned) shape. This facilitates the application of boundary conditions on the outer surfaces.

### Element Definitions
- Define cell block names corresponding to each of the three regions (casing, cement sheath, and rock)
- Specify appropriate element types for each cell block region

## Material Properties and Constitutive Models

### Constitutive Model Type
Use the isotropic linear elastic constitutive model ("ElasticIsotropic") for all three materials.

### Material Definitions
Define three separate materials:

1. **Steel** (for casing): Specify elastic properties using appropriate Lamé parameters or equivalent elastic moduli (Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio). Steel typically has high stiffness values.

2. **Cement** (for cement sheath): Specify elastic properties appropriate for wellbore cement material.

3. **Rock** (for formation): Specify elastic properties appropriate for the surrounding rock formation.

Note: While density values must be provided for each material definition, they are not utilized in this quasi-static elastic analysis.

## Boundary Conditions

### Far-Field Boundary Constraints
Apply roller boundary conditions on the far-field boundaries. These constraints prevent normal displacement while allowing tangential movement along the outer surfaces of the domain.

### Internal Pressure Loading
Configure a traction boundary condition on the inner surface of the casing:
- **Target surface**: Apply to the nodeset named "rneg" which is automatically generated by the internal wellbore mesh generator for the inner casing face
- **Traction type**: Set to "normal" to simulate a casing pressure test where pressure acts perpendicular to the inner casing surface
- **Magnitude and sign**: Specify the pressure magnitude with a negative scale value. The negative sign is required because GEOS uses a negative sign convention for compressive stresses, and the applied pressure represents a compressive load on the casing interior.

## Initial Conditions

No specific initial stress or displacement conditions are described for this problem. The simulation begins from an unstressed reference state.

## Numerical Method Specifications

The simulation employs the Lagrangian finite element method for spatial discretization of the solid mechanics equations. The problem is linear elastic, so it should converge in a single iteration without requiring nonlinear solver settings.

## Output Requirements

The simulation should output results that allow for extraction and visualization of:
- Radial stress component (σ_rr) throughout all three regions
- Hoop stress component (σ_θθ) throughout all three regions
- Displacement fields for validation

Results should be extractable along radial profiles to compare against the analytical solution based on the Hervé and Zaoui (1995) formulation for multi-layer cylinders.

## File Organization

The configuration should be organized into base and benchmark XML files:
- A base file containing common definitions (constitutive laws, boundary conditions)
- A benchmark file containing solver and mesh specifications specific to the validation study

The files should be structured to allow inclusion/referencing between them for modularity.
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>

  <Events
    maxTime="1.0">
    <!-- This event is applied every cycle, and overrides the
    solver time-step request -->
    <!-- SPHINX_Execution -->
    <PeriodicEvent
      name="solverApplications"
      forceDt="0.1"
      target="/Solvers/lagsolve"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_ExecutionEnd -->
    <!-- This event is applied every 5.0e-5s.  The targetExactTimestep
    flag allows this event to request a dt modification to match an
    integer multiple of the timeFrequency. -->
    <PeriodicEvent
      name="outputs"
      timeFrequency="1.0"
      targetExactTimestep="1"
      target="/Outputs/siloOutput"/>

    <PeriodicEvent
      name="restarts"
      timeFrequency="1.0"
      targetExactTimestep="0"
      target="/Outputs/restartOutput"/>
  </Events>

  <!-- SPHINX_FEDiscretization -->
  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <!-- SPHINX_FEDiscretizationEnd -->
  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="casing"
      cellBlocks="{ casing }"
      materialList="{ casing }"/>
      
    <CellElementRegion
      name="cement"
      cellBlocks="{ cement }"
      materialList="{ cement }"/>

    <CellElementRegion
      name="rock"
      cellBlocks="{ rock }"
      materialList="{ rock }"/>
      
  </ElementRegions>

  <Constitutive>
    <!-- SPHINX_Material -->
    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="casing"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="175e9"
      defaultShearModulus="80.8e9"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="cement"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="10.3e9"
      defaultShearModulus="6.45e9"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="rock"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="5.5556e9"
      defaultShearModulus="4.16667e9"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_MaterialEnd -->
  </Constitutive>

  <!-- SPHINX_BoundaryConditions -->
  <FieldSpecifications>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="xConstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ xneg, xpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="yConstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ yneg, ypos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="zconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ zneg, zpos }"/>

    <Traction
      name="innerPressure"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      tractionType="normal"
      scale="-10.0e6"
      setNames="{ rneg }"/>
  </FieldSpecifications>

  <!-- SPHINX_BoundaryConditionsEnd -->
  <!-- SPHINX_TableFunction -->
  <!--Functions>
    <TableFunction
      name="timeFunction"
      inputVarNames="{ time }"
      coordinates="{ 0.0, 1.0, 10.0 }"
      values=     "{ 0.0, 0.0, 10.0 }"/>
  </Functions-->

  <!-- SPHINX_TableFunctionEnd -->
  <Outputs>
    <Silo
      name="siloOutput"
      parallelThreads="32"
      plotFileRoot="plot"
      childDirectory="sub"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>
</Problem>

title: .. _AdvancedWellboreExampleNonLinearThermalDiffusionTemperatureDependentVolumetricHeatCapacity:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Non-Linear Thermal Diffusion Around a Wellbore XML Configuration

## Overview and Simulation Type

Create an XML configuration file for a **non-linear thermal diffusion simulation** around a wellbore geometry. This simulation models heat transfer in porous rock surrounding a wellbore where the volumetric heat capacity of the solid rock varies linearly with temperature. The simulation uses a **thermal single-phase flow solver** to capture the coupled thermal-hydraulic behavior.

This is a 2D axisymmetric or radial problem centered on a wellbore.

## Solver Configuration

Configure a **thermal compressible single-phase flow solver** with the following requirements:

- The solver must be capable of handling non-linear thermal diffusion problems
- Enable thermal effects in the single-phase flow formulation
- The solver should account for temperature-dependent material properties
- Configure the solver to use appropriate non-linear iteration schemes since the volumetric heat capacity introduces non-linearity through its temperature dependence

## Mesh Requirements

The mesh should represent a 2D domain around a wellbore:

- Use a radial or annular mesh geometry extending outward from the wellbore wall
- The inner boundary represents the wellbore surface
- The outer boundary should be far enough to approximate infinite medium conditions
- Element type should be appropriate for 2D thermal analysis (likely quadrilateral elements)
- Mesh refinement should be concentrated near the wellbore where temperature gradients are steepest

## Constitutive Models

### Solid Internal Energy Model (Critical Component)

This is the key constitutive specification for this example. Define a **SolidInternalEnergy** model with temperature-dependent volumetric heat capacity:

- Specify a **reference volumetric heat capacity** value for the rock medium
- Define the **derivative of volumetric heat capacity with respect to temperature** (dVolumetricHeatCapacity_dTemperature) to capture the linear temperature dependence
- The relationship should be: volumetric heat capacity = reference value + (derivative × temperature change)

### Additional Constitutive Models

- Define thermal conductivity properties for the rock medium
- Specify fluid properties if the single-phase flow component is active
- Include rock porosity and permeability properties as required by the thermal single-phase flow solver
- Define rock compressibility and thermal expansion coefficients

## Material Properties

For the rock/solid medium surrounding the wellbore:

- Reference volumetric heat capacity (specify the base value at reference temperature)
- Temperature derivative of volumetric heat capacity (captures the linear dependence)
- Thermal conductivity of the solid matrix
- Density of the solid rock

For any fluid phase present:

- Fluid thermal properties
- Fluid density and compressibility

## Initial Conditions

- Specify an initial temperature distribution throughout the domain (typically uniform far-field temperature)
- Define initial pressure conditions if required by the thermal single-phase solver

## Boundary Conditions

### Wellbore Boundary (Inner Boundary)

- Apply a thermal boundary condition at the wellbore wall (either prescribed temperature or heat flux)
- This represents the thermal perturbation source for the diffusion problem

### Far-Field Boundary (Outer Boundary)

- Apply appropriate far-field conditions (typically constant temperature representing undisturbed formation temperature)
- May use large domain extent to approximate infinite boundary conditions

## Numerical Method Specifications

- Configure time-stepping appropriate for transient thermal diffusion
- Set up non-linear solver tolerances to handle the temperature-dependent heat capacity
- Newton-Raphson or similar iterative scheme may be required due to material non-linearity
- Specify convergence criteria for the non-linear iterations

## Output Requirements

- Record temperature field at specified time intervals
- Output should enable comparison with analytical or finite difference reference solutions
- Include radial temperature profiles from wellbore outward at various time steps
- Results should be suitable for generating temperature vs. radial distance plots at different times for validation against classical finite difference method solutions

## File Structure

The configuration should be organized to potentially use two XML files:

1. A **base configuration file** containing the fundamental 2D thermal compressible flow setup, mesh definition, and general solver parameters
2. A **benchmark-specific file** that includes or overrides settings specific to the temperature-dependent volumetric heat capacity case, particularly the SolidInternalEnergy constitutive definition with the non-linear (temperature-dependent) parameters
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <Solvers>
    <SinglePhaseFVM
      name="singleFlow"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="tpfaFlow"
      temperature="0"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ region }">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-6"
        newtonMaxIter="100"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"/>
    </SinglePhaseFVM>
  </Solvers>

  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteVolume>
      <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="tpfaFlow"/>
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <Constitutive>

    <CompressibleSolidConstantPermeability
      name="rock_linear"
      solidModelName="nullSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy_linear"/>

    <CompressibleSolidConstantPermeability
      name="rock_temperatureDependentVolumetricHeatCapacity"
      solidModelName="nullSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy_nonLinear"/>

    <NullModel
      name="nullSolid"/>

    <PressurePorosity
      name="rockPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="0.1"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      compressibility="3.0e-11"/>

	<!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_linear -->
    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="rockInternalEnergy_linear"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="1.0e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_linearEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_nonLinear -->
    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="rockInternalEnergy_nonLinear"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="4.56e6"
      dVolumetricHeatCapacity_dTemperature="1e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_nonLinearEnd -->

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="rockPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-18, 1.0e-18, 1.0e-18 }"/>

	<!-- SPHINX_ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid -->
    <ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid
      name="fluid"
      defaultDensity="1000"
      defaultViscosity="0.001"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      compressibility="5e-10"
      thermalExpansionCoeff="3e-4"
      viscosibility="0.0"
      specificHeatCapacity="1"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0.99"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluidEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_linear -->
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="thermalCond_linear"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.66, 1.66, 1.66 }"
      thermalConductivityGradientComponents="{ 0, 0, 0 }"
      referenceTemperature="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_linearEnd -->    

	<!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_nonLinear -->
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="thermalCond_nonLinear"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.5, 1.5, 1.5 }"
      thermalConductivityGradientComponents="{ -12e-4, -12e-4, -12e-4 }"
      referenceTemperature="20"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_nonLinearEnd -->    
	
  </Constitutive>

  <FieldSpecifications>

	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedPressure -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialPressure"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/region/cb"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkPressure"
      setNames="{ rpos }"       
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sourcePressure"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedPressureEnd -->

	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedTemperature -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialTemperature"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/region/cb"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkTemperature"
      setNames="{ rpos }"       
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sourceTemperature"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="-20.0"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedTemperatureEnd -->

  </FieldSpecifications>

  <Outputs>
    <VTK
      name="vtkOutput"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>
</Problem>

title: .. _AdvancedExampleThermoPoroElasticWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for ThermoPoroElastic Wellbore Simulation

## 1. Simulation Type and Physical Problem

This simulation models a thermoporoelastic open wellbore problem using GEOS. The physical scenario involves a wellbore drilled through a rock formation that is subjected to a uniform temperature change applied on its inner surface. The rock formation exhibits isotropic linear thermoporoelastic behavior. The problem assumes plane strain conditions (no deformation along the wellbore axis) and axisymmetric conditions (quarter symmetry).

The solver to use is the **SinglePhasePoromechanics** solver with the **thermal option enabled**. This solver couples solid mechanics, single-phase fluid flow, and heat transfer. Gravitational effects should be ignored in this simulation. The coupling should be fully coupled (not one-way coupling).

## 2. Mesh Requirements

Use the **InternalWellbore** internal mesh generator to create the computational domain.

### Geometric Parameters:
- Define a **radius vector** specifying the inner wellbore radius and the far-field boundary radius of the surrounding rock formation
- Set the **theta** angle range from **0 to 90 degrees** to model a quarter of the wellbore geometry (exploiting axisymmetric symmetry)
- Define a **vertical well trajectory** (the trajectory coordinates should specify a vertical orientation)
- Model only a **single horizontal layer** since plane strain conditions apply and thermal diffusion occurs only along the radial direction

### Mesh Optimization:
- Enable the **autoSpaceRadialElems** parameter to automatically optimize element sizing, with smaller elements near the wellbore and progressively larger elements toward the far-field boundary
- This creates a radially-graded mesh that captures the steep gradients near the wellbore while maintaining computational efficiency

## 3. Material Properties and Constitutive Models

### Thermoelastic Solid Properties:
Define the following properties within a thermoelastic constitutive model:
- **Drained bulk elastic modulus** (K)
- **Drained shear elastic modulus** (G)
- **Drained linear thermal expansion coefficient** (α) - relates stress change to temperature variation
- **Solid density** - must be defined even though gravitational effects are ignored

### Poroelastic Properties:
Define porosity and skeleton properties:
- **Porosity** of the rock formation
- **Elastic bulk modulus of the solid skeleton** (Ks) - the intrinsic grain bulk modulus

### Thermal Properties:
Specify two separate property sets:
- **Thermal conductivity** of the rock formation
- **Volumetric heat capacity** of the rock formation

### Permeability Properties:
- Define the **permeability** of the rock formation (isotropic)

### Fluid Properties:
Define a fluid model with:
- **Viscosity**
- **Thermal expansion coefficient** of the fluid
- **Compressibility** or bulk modulus
- **Volumetric heat capacity** - set to a **negligible value** to ignore thermal convection effects; this ensures that only thermal diffusion (conduction) is considered in the heat transfer

## 4. Initial Conditions

### Initial Stress State:
- Set **initial effective stresses** consistent with the initial temperature change using the relationship: σ₀ = 3Kα·δT₀, where σ₀ is the initial effective principal stress, K is the drained bulk modulus, α is the drained linear thermal expansion coefficient, and δT₀ is the initial temperature change
- If the initial temperature change is **zero**, then the initial effective stresses should be set to **zero**

### Initial Temperature:
- Define the **initial temperature field** throughout the domain (this also serves as the far-field reference temperature)

### Initial Pore Pressure:
- Set the **initial pore pressure** distribution throughout the rock formation

## 5. Boundary Conditions

### Mechanical Boundary Conditions for Axisymmetric Plane Strain:
- Apply **symmetry conditions** on the theta = 0 degree face (constrain displacement normal to this face)
- Apply **symmetry conditions** on the theta = 90 degree face (constrain displacement normal to this face)
- These conditions enforce the axisymmetric behavior

### Far-Field Boundary (Outer Radius):
- Apply **fixed displacement** boundary condition (all displacement components constrained to zero)
- This represents the assumption that local changes near the wellbore have negligible effect at the far-field boundary

### Wellbore Inner Surface:
- Apply **traction-free** boundary condition (zero traction/stress on the inner surface)
- This represents an open, unsupported wellbore

### Temperature Boundary Conditions:
- Apply a **temperature Dirichlet condition** on the inner wellbore surface specifying the changed temperature
- The far-field boundary temperature should remain at the **initial temperature value**

### Pore Pressure Boundary Conditions:
- Define **pore pressure conditions** on the inner wellbore surface
- Define **pore pressure conditions** at the far-field boundary
- Specify both initial values and boundary conditions for pressure

## 6. Numerical Method Specifications

### Solver Configuration:
- Use the **SinglePhasePoromechanics** solver
- Enable the **thermal** option/capability
- Configure for **fully coupled** thermoporomechanical analysis

### Time Stepping:
- Define appropriate time stepping parameters for the transient thermal diffusion problem
- Set up periodic events to trigger output collection throughout the simulation duration

## 7. Output Requirements

### Output Format:
- Use **HDF5 format** for output data to facilitate post-processing with Python

### Field Data Collection:
Configure the following field data collectors:

1. **Temperature Field:**
   - Create a PackCollection object to collect temperature data
   - Create a corresponding TimeHistory task to write the temperature collection
   - Collect for all time steps

2. **Effective Stress Field:**
   - Create a PackCollection object to collect solid stress data from the element region
   - Create a corresponding TimeHistory task for stress output
   - Collect stress components across the entire domain

3. **Displacement Field:**
   - Create a PackCollection object targeting the **nodeManager** to collect displacement data
   - Create a corresponding TimeHistory task for displacement output

### Periodic Events:
- Define **PeriodicEvent** objects to trigger data collection at regular intervals throughout the simulation
- Ensure events are linked to the appropriate collection and output tasks
- Set appropriate time intervals that capture the transient behavior adequately

## File Organization Note

The configuration may be split into two XML files:
1. A **base file** containing material properties, boundary conditions, constitutive definitions, and output specifications
2. A **benchmark file** containing mesh definition, time events, and simulation-specific parameters that includes/references the base file
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <Solvers>
    <SinglePhasePoromechanics
      name="THMSolver"
      solidSolverName="solidMechSolver"
      flowSolverName="flowSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ rock }">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        couplingType="FullyImplicit"
        newtonMaxIter="100"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        solverType="direct"/>
    </SinglePhasePoromechanics>

    <SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM
      name="solidMechSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="FE1"
      targetRegions="{ rock }">
    </SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM>
   
    <SinglePhaseFVM
      name="flowSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="tpfaFlow"
      temperature="0"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ rock }">
    </SinglePhaseFVM>
  </Solvers>

  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>

    <FiniteVolume>
      <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="tpfaFlow"/>
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="rock"
      cellBlocks="{ * }"
      materialList="{ fluid, rock, rockThermalCond }"/>
  </ElementRegions>

  <Constitutive>
    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="rock"
      solidModelName="rockSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_PoroElasticProperties -->
    <BiotPorosity
      name="rockPorosity"

    <!-- SPHINX_PorePressureBC -->
    <FieldSpecification

      objectPath="ElementRegions"

    <FieldSpecification

  <Tasks>

    <PackCollection

    <!-- SPHINX_PressureCollection -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="stressCollection_rock"

      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressCollectionEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="displacementCollection"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollectionEnd -->

  </Tasks>

  <Outputs>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="temperatureHistoryOutput_rock"
      sources="{ /Tasks/temperatureCollection_rock }"
      filename="temperatureHistory_rock"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_PressureTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="pressureHistoryOutput_rock"
      sources="{ /Tasks/pressureCollection_rock }"

    <!-- SPHINX_PressureTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory

      sources="{ /Tasks/stressCollection_rock }"
      filename="stressHistory_rock"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolidStressTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="displacementHistoryOutput"
      sources="{ /Tasks/displacementCollection }"
      filename="displacementHistory"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <VTK
      name="vtkOutput"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>
</Problem>

natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Cased ThermoElastic Wellbore with Imperfect Contact Interfaces

## Overview and Simulation Type

Create a GEOS XML configuration file for simulating a coupled Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical (THM) problem involving a cased wellbore with imperfect (debonding) contact interfaces. The physical scenario models cold CO2 injection causing temperature reduction at the casing surface. The simulation must allow for debonding (separation) at both the casing-cement and cement-rock interfaces.

The configuration should be split into two XML files: a base file containing the core solver definitions, material properties, and boundary conditions, and a benchmark file containing geometry specifications and interface definitions.

## Physical Problem Description

The wellbore system consists of three concentric layers:
1. Steel casing (innermost)
2. Cement sheath (middle)
3. Rock formation (outermost)

All three materials exhibit isotropic linear thermo-elastic behavior. Heat transfer occurs only through conduction (no convection or fluid flow). The problem is treated as an axisymmetric plane strain problem.

## Solver Configuration

Configure a coupled THM solver that handles imperfect contact interfaces. The solver requires:

1. **Primary Solver**: A coupled THM solver that combines thermal and solid mechanics solutions with contact mechanics
2. **Lagrangian Contact Solver**: For handling mechanical contact at the imperfect interfaces, allowing separation/debonding between layers
3. **THM Coupled Solver**: For solving the thermo-elastic coupling between temperature changes and mechanical deformation

The solver must be capable of tracking displacement jumps across contact interfaces and computing temperature-induced stresses.

## Mesh Requirements

Define a wellbore mesh with the following characteristics:
- Geometry: Cylindrical/axisymmetric representation of the wellbore
- Three distinct regions corresponding to casing, cement sheath, and rock formation
- Use Cylinder geometry objects to define nodesets for selecting the imperfect interface locations between:
  - Casing and cement (inner interface)
  - Cement and rock (outer interface)
- The mesh should be refined enough to capture the thermal and mechanical gradients near the interfaces

## Material Properties

### Solid Materials (Casing, Cement, Rock)
Define THM properties for three materials, all using isotropic linear thermo-elastic constitutive models:

1. **Steel Casing**: Define elastic modulus, Poisson's ratio, thermal expansion coefficient, thermal conductivity, and density appropriate for steel
2. **Cement Sheath**: Define elastic modulus, Poisson's ratio, thermal expansion coefficient, thermal conductivity, and density appropriate for wellbore cement
3. **Rock Formation**: Define elastic modulus, Poisson's ratio, thermal expansion coefficient, thermal conductivity, and density appropriate for the surrounding rock

### Contact Interface Properties
Define properties for the imperfect contact surfaces at both interfaces:

1. **Mechanical Contact Properties**: Specify contact stiffness and friction parameters for Lagrangian contact formulation
2. **Thermal Conductivity of Contact Interfaces**: Define thermal conductivity properties specifically for the contact interfaces to model heat transfer across potentially debonded surfaces
3. **Flow Properties for Contact Surfaces**: Although no actual flow is modeled, the fully coupled THM solver requires flow property definitions for the contact surfaces

### Surface Element Region
Define a surface element region that uses the contact interface properties, associating the thermal and mechanical properties with the interface elements.

## Initial Conditions

Specify in-situ initial conditions including:
- Initial temperature distribution throughout the domain (casing, cement, and rock)
- Initial stress state in all three materials
- Any required initial conditions for the contact interfaces

## Boundary Conditions

### Thermal Boundary Conditions
1. **Casing Inner Surface**: Apply a temperature reduction boundary condition representing cold CO2 injection (this is the driving force for the thermal problem)
2. **Far-field Boundary**: Apply appropriate far-field temperature boundary condition on the outer boundary of the rock formation domain

### Mechanical Boundary Conditions
1. **Casing Inner Surface**: Define any mechanical constraints or pressure conditions at the inner wellbore surface
2. **Far-field Boundary**: Apply far-field stress or displacement boundary conditions on the outer boundary
3. **Contact Surface Specifications**: Define contact boundary conditions that allow for debonding/separation at both the casing-cement and cement-rock interfaces

## Time Stepping and Numerical Parameters

Configure the simulation to run to a final time of 1e5 seconds (100,000 seconds). Include appropriate:
- Time step sizes for the coupled THM problem
- Nonlinear solver tolerances for contact convergence
- Linear solver parameters suitable for the coupled system

## Output Requirements

Configure outputs to capture:
1. **Displacement Jump**: Track displacement discontinuities across both the casing-cement and cement-rock interfaces
2. **Temperature Field**: Output temperature distribution throughout the wellbore system
3. **Radial Displacement**: Output the radial displacement field around the wellbore
4. **Stress Components**: Output total radial stress and hoop stress (tangential stress) components

Results should be available for comparison with analytical solutions at the final simulation time of 1e5 seconds.

## File Organization

The configuration should be organized as:
1. **Base XML File** (CasedThermoElasticWellbore_ImperfectInterfaces_base.xml): Contains solver definitions, material properties including contact thermal properties, contact flow properties, surface element region definitions, and boundary/initial conditions
2. **Benchmark XML File** (CasedThermoElasticWellbore_ImperfectInterfaces_benchmark.xml): Contains geometry and mesh definitions, interface nodeset selections using Cylinder geometry objects, and includes/references the base file

The benchmark file should include the base file to inherit all solver and material definitions while specifying the specific geometry for the validation problem.
