<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <Solvers>
    <!-- SPHINX_ContactTHMSolver -->
    <SinglePhasePoromechanicsConformingFractures
      name="fractureThermoPoroElasticSolver"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock, Fracture }"
      initialDt="1e-3"
      flowSolverName="flowSolver"
      solidSolverName="lagrangiancontact"
      logLevel="1"
      isThermal="1">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-5"
        newtonMaxIter="10"
        maxTimeStepCuts="4"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"
        solverType="direct"/>
    </SinglePhasePoromechanicsConformingFractures>
    <!-- SPHINX_ContactTHMSolverEnd -->

    <SolidMechanicsLagrangeContact
      name="lagrangiancontact"
      stabilizationName="contactStabilization"
      discretization="FE1"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock, Fracture }"
      logLevel="1">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-6"
        logLevel="2"
        newtonMaxIter="10"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"/>
    </SolidMechanicsLagrangeContact>


    <SinglePhaseFVM
      name="flowSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="tpfaFlow"
      temperature="0"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock, Fracture }">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
	    normType="L2"/>
    </SinglePhaseFVM>

    <!-- SPHINX_SolversSurfaceGenerator -->
    <SurfaceGenerator
      name="SurfaceGen"
      fractureRegion="Fracture"
      targetRegions="{ casing, cement, rock }"
      initialRockToughness="1.0e6"
      mpiCommOrder="1"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolversSurfaceGeneratorEnd -->
  </Solvers>

  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>

    <FiniteVolume>
    <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="tpfaFlow"/>
    <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="contactStabilization"/>    
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <ElementRegions>
    <!-- SPHINX_SurfaceElementRegion -->   
    <SurfaceElementRegion
      name="Fracture"
      faceBlock="faceElementSubRegion"
      materialList="{ fluid, fractureFilling, frictionLaw, contactThermalCond, hApertureModel }"
      defaultAperture="5.0e-4"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SurfaceElementRegionEnd -->  

    <CellElementRegion
      name="casing"
      cellBlocks="{ casing }"
      materialList="{ fluid, casing, casingThermalCond }"/>

    <CellElementRegion
      name="cement"
      cellBlocks="{ cement }"
      materialList="{ fluid, cement, cementThermalCond }"/>

    <CellElementRegion
      name="rock"
      cellBlocks="{ rock }"
      materialList="{ fluid, rock, rockThermalCond }"/>
  </ElementRegions>

  <Constitutive>
    <Coulomb
      name="frictionLaw"
      cohesion="0"
      frictionCoefficient="0.5"/>

    <HydraulicApertureTable
      name="hApertureModel"
      apertureTableName="apertureTable"/>   

    <!-- SPHINX_ContactFlowProperties -->
    <CompressibleSolidParallelPlatesPermeability
      name="fractureFilling"
      solidModelName="nullSolid"
      porosityModelName="fracturePorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="fracturePerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy"/>

    <NullModel
      name="nullSolid"/>

    <PressurePorosity
      name="fracturePorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1.00"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      compressibility="0.0"/>

    <ParallelPlatesPermeability
      name="fracturePerm"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ContactFlowPropertiesEnd -->

    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="casing"
      solidModelName="casingSolid"
      porosityModelName="casingPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="casingPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="casingInternalEnergy"/>

    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="cement"
      solidModelName="cementSolid"
      porosityModelName="cementPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="cementPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="cementInternalEnergy"/>

    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="rock"
      solidModelName="rockSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_PoroElasticProperties -->
    <BiotPorosity
      name="casingPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1e-6"
      defaultGrainBulkModulus="159.4202899e9"/>

    <BiotPorosity
      name="cementPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1e-6"
      defaultGrainBulkModulus="2.298850575e9"/>

    <BiotPorosity
      name="rockPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="1e-6"
      defaultGrainBulkModulus="5.535714286e9"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_PoroElasticPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_HeatCapacityProperties -->
    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="casingInternalEnergy"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="1.375e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>

    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="cementInternalEnergy"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="4.2e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>

    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="rockInternalEnergy"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="4.56e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_HeatCapacityPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_PermeabilityProperties -->
    <ConstantPermeability
      name="casingPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100 }"/>

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="cementPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100 }"/>

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="rockPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100, 1.0e-100 }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_PermeabilityPropertiesEnd -->

    
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="casingThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 15, 15, 15 }"/>

    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="cementThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 }"/>

    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="rockThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.66, 1.66, 1.66 }"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_ContactThermalProperties -->
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="contactThermalCond"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ContactThermalPropertiesEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_FluidProperties -->
    <ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid
      name="fluid"
      defaultDensity="1000"
      defaultViscosity="1e-3"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      referenceTemperature="20.0"
      compressibility="5e-10"
      thermalExpansionCoeff="1e-10"
      viscosibility="0.0"
      specificHeatCapacity="1"
      referenceInternalEnergy="1"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_FluidPropertiesEnd -->

	<!-- SPHINX_ThermoElasticProperties -->
    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="casingSolid"
      defaultDensity="7500"
      defaultBulkModulus="159.4202899e9"
      defaultShearModulus="86.61417323e9"
      defaultDrainedLinearTEC="1.2e-5"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="cementSolid"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="2.298850575e9"
      defaultShearModulus="1.652892562e9"
      defaultDrainedLinearTEC="2.0e-5"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="rockSolid"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="5.535714286e9"
      defaultShearModulus="3.81147541e9"
      defaultDrainedLinearTEC="2.0e-5"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ThermoElasticPropertiesEnd -->
    
  </Constitutive>

  <FieldSpecifications>
   <!-- SPHINX_ContactBoundaryConditions -->
   <FieldSpecification
      name="frac"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ casingCementInterface, cementRockInterface }"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="ruptureState"
      scale="1"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="separableFace"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ casingCementInterface, cementRockInterface }"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="isFaceSeparable"
      scale="1"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ContactBoundaryConditionsEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_FixedFarFieldBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="rPosConstraint_x"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ rpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="rPosConstraint_y"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ rpos }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_FixedFarFieldBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_PlaneStrainAxisymmetryBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="tNegConstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tneg }"/>

   <FieldSpecification
      name="tPosConstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="zconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ zneg, zpos }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_PlaneStrainAxisymmetryBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_StressCasingInit -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_x_casing"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_y_casing"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_z_casing"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="casingSolid_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_StressCasingInit -->

    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_x_cement"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_y_cement"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_z_cement"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/cement/cement"
      fieldName="cementSolid_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_x_rock"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_y_rock"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"/>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialSigma_z_rock"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/rock/rock"
      fieldName="rockSolid_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroPorePressureBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="zeroPressure"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sourcePressure"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkPressure"
      setNames="{ rpos }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroPorePressureBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureBC -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialTemperature"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="farfieldTemperature"
      setNames="{ rpos }"       
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="innerTemperature"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="-20.0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureBCEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroInnerTractionBC -->
    <Traction
      name="innerPressure"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      tractionType="normal"
      scale="0.0e6"
      setNames="{ rneg }"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_ZeroInnerTractionBCEnd -->

  </FieldSpecifications>

  <!-- SPHINX_TableFunction -->
  <Functions>
    <TableFunction
      name="ForceTimeFunction"
      inputVarNames="{ time }"
      coordinates="{ 0.0, 0.5, 2.0 }"
      values="{ 0.0, -1.0, 1.0 }"/>
    <TableFunction
      name="apertureTable"
      coordinates="{ -1.0e-3, 0.0 }"
      values="{ 1e-4, 1e-3 }"/> 
  </Functions>
  <!-- SPHINX_TableFunctionEnd -->

  <Tasks>

    <!-- SPHINX_TemperatureCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="temperatureCollection_casing"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/casing/casing"
      fieldName="temperature"/>
    <PackCollection
      name="temperatureCollection_cement"

title: .. _ExampleKirschWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Kirsch Wellbore Problem XML Configuration

## Overview and Simulation Type

Create an XML configuration file for a three-dimensional vertical elastic wellbore simulation known as the Kirsch Wellbore Problem. This is a solid mechanics problem that models a drained wellbore subjected to anisotropic in-situ horizontal stresses and internal wellbore pressure. The simulation computes the elastic deformation and stress concentration in the near-wellbore region of an infinite, homogeneous, isotropic, elastic medium. A plane strain condition should be applied. The purpose is to verify numerical results against the analytical Kirsch solution for stress and displacement fields around a circular cavity.

## Solver Configuration

### Primary Solver
Configure a solid mechanics solver using the Lagrangian finite element formulation (SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM). The solver should be named "mechanicsSolver" and configured for quasi-static analysis, meaning inertial effects are not considered. Since this is a drained wellbore problem, pore pressure variations are omitted and only mechanical deformation is solved.

### Solver Parameters
- Solver type: SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM
- Solver name: mechanicsSolver
- Problem type: QuasiStatic
- Discretization method: Reference a finite element discretization named "FE1"
- Target region material: Reference material named "rock"

## Numerical Methods

Define a finite element discretization in the NumericalMethods section. Create a discretization scheme named "FE1" that will be referenced by the solid mechanics solver. This discretization should be compatible with eight-node hexahedral elements (C3D8).

## Mesh Specification

### Mesh Generator
Use the internal wellbore mesh generator (InternalWellbore) to create the computational domain.

### Domain Dimensions
- Total domain size: 10 meters × 5 meters × 2 meters (radial extent × width × height)
- Initial wellbore radius (a₀): 0.1 meters

### Angular Configuration
- Theta angle range: 0 to 180 degrees
- This models half of the wellbore domain, assuming symmetry for the remaining portion

### Wellbore Trajectory
Define the trajectory coordinates to create a vertical wellbore (the wellbore axis aligned with the z-direction).

### Mesh Refinement Settings
- Enable automatic radial element spacing by setting autoSpaceRadialElems to "{1}" - this automatically determines the number and spacing of elements in the radial direction, overriding manual nr values
- Set useCartesianOuterBoundary to "0" to enforce a Cartesian-aligned boundary condition on the outer blocks

### Element Configuration
- Total elements: 50 elements in radial direction × 40 elements in tangential direction × 2 elements in z-direction
- Element type: Eight-node hexahedral elements (C3D8)
- The mesh should include refinement to conform with the wellbore geometry
- Define the mesh as a cell block named "cb1"

## Constitutive Models and Material Properties

### Material Model
Use an isotropic linear elastic constitutive model (ElasticIsotropic) to simulate the mechanical behavior of the rock.

### Material Name
Name the material "rock" to match the reference in the solver configuration.

### Material Properties (in SI Units - International System of Units)
- Bulk Modulus (K): 500.0 MPa (500.0e6 Pa)
- Shear Modulus (G): 300.0 MPa (300.0e6 Pa)
- Density: Specify an appropriate rock density value in kg/m³

## Initial Conditions

All initial condition fields must have the initialCondition attribute set to "1".

### Initial Stress State
Apply anisotropic in-situ stresses throughout the domain:
- Minimum horizontal stress (σyy): -9.0 MPa (-9.0e6 Pa)
- Maximum horizontal stress (σxx): -11.25 MPa (-11.25e6 Pa)
- Vertical stress (σzz): -15.0 MPa (-15.0e6 Pa)

Note: Negative values indicate compressive stresses following GEOS sign convention.

## Boundary Conditions

### Wellbore Wall Loading
- Apply a normal traction named "WellLoad" on the wellbore wall surface (identified as "rneg")
- Traction type: "normal"
- Magnitude (Pw): -2.0 MPa (scale value: -2.0e6 Pa)
- The traction is computed as the scalar product of the scale value and the outward face normal vector
- This represents a compressive mud pressure or internal supporting pressure
- The loading magnitude remains constant with time

### Outer Boundary Constraints
Apply roller constraints (zero displacement normal to the boundary) on the remaining outer boundaries:
- xneg: Left-most face in x-direction
- xpos: Right-most face in x-direction
- yneg: Bottom face in y-direction
- ypos: Top face in y-direction
- zneg: Back face in z-direction
- zpos: Front face in z-direction

### Field Specification Notes
- Use objectPath "nodeManager" for displacement boundary conditions applied to element nodes
- Use objectPath "faceManager" for traction boundary conditions applied to element faces
- Component indices: 0 = x-direction, 1 = y-direction, 2 = z-direction
- Use fieldName to reference registered GEOS fields

## Output Requirements

### VTK Output
Configure VTK output files for visualization in Paraview to display stress distributions (particularly σxx) in the near-wellbore region.

### Time History Output
Configure the Tasks section with PackCollection tasks to collect time history information:

1. **Stress Collection Task**
   - Task name: stressCollection
   - Collect the "averageStress" field
   - This outputs a tensor stored as an array with Voigt notation (6 components per cell)
   - The averageStress represents cell-wise average of each stress component calculated using finite element quadrature rule

2. **Displacement Collection Task**
   - Task name: displacementCollection
   - Collect the "totalDisplacement" field
   - This outputs a 3-component vector representing the displacement field

### Events Configuration
Define PeriodicEvent entries in the Events section to trigger the stress and displacement collection tasks at recurring intervals.

### Output Files
Configure output to generate HDF5 formatted files:
- displacement_history.hdf5
- stress_history.hdf5

These files should contain datasets for:
- Simulation time
- Element center or nodal positions
- The collected time history information for stress and displacement fields

## File Structure

The configuration should be structured to potentially use two files:
1. A base configuration file containing solver, constitutive, field specifications, and tasks
2. A benchmark configuration file containing the mesh definition

The benchmark file can include or reference the base file to create the complete simulation setup.
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>


<Problem>
<!-- SPHINX_MATERIAL -->
  <Constitutive>
    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="rock"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="5.0e8"
      defaultShearModulus="3.0e8"
    />
  </Constitutive>
<!-- SPHINX_MATERIAL_END -->

<!--Assign material to geometry parts-->
  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion 
      name="Omega" 
      cellBlocks="{ * }" 
      materialList="{ rock }"
    />
  </ElementRegions>

<!-- SPHINX_BC -->
  <FieldSpecifications>
    <FieldSpecification 
      name="Sxx"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="-11.25e6"
    />

    <FieldSpecification 
      name="Syy"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="-9.0e6"
    />

    <FieldSpecification 
      name="Szz"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="-15.0e6"
    />

    <Traction
      name="WellLoad"
      setNames="{ rneg }"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      scale="-2.0e6"
      tractionType="normal"      
    />
  
    <FieldSpecification 
      name="xconstraint"    
      objectPath="nodeManager" 
      fieldName="totalDisplacement" 
      component="0" 
      scale="0.0" 
      setNames="{xneg, xpos}"
    />

    <FieldSpecification 
      name="yconstraint"    
      objectPath="nodeManager" 
      fieldName="totalDisplacement" 
      component="1" 
      scale="0.0" 
      setNames="{tneg, tpos, ypos}"
    />

    <FieldSpecification 
      name="zconstraint" 
      objectPath="nodeManager" 
      fieldName="totalDisplacement" 
      component="2" 
      scale="0.0" 
      setNames="{zneg, zpos}"
    />  
  </FieldSpecifications>
<!-- SPHINX_BC_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_TASKS -->
  <Tasks>
    <PackCollection
      name="stressCollection"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
      fieldName="averageStress"/>
      
    <PackCollection
      name="displacementCollection"
      objectPath="nodeManager" 
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"/>      
  </Tasks>
<!-- SPHINX_TASKS_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_OUTPUT -->
  <Outputs>
    <VTK 
      name="vtkOutput"
      plotFileRoot="plot"
    />

    <TimeHistory
      name="stressOutput"
      sources="{/Tasks/stressCollection}"
      filename="stress_history" />
      
    <TimeHistory
      name="displacementOutput"
      sources="{/Tasks/displacementCollection}"
      filename="displacement_history" />
      
    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>  
  </Outputs>
<!-- SPHINX_OUTPUT_END -->

<!-- SPHINX_SOLVER -->
  <Solvers gravityVector="{0.0, 0.0, 0.0}">
    <SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM 
      name="mechanicsSolver" 
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="FE1"
      targetRegions="{Omega}">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol = "1.0e-5"
        newtonMaxIter = "15"
      />
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"/>
    </SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM>
  </Solvers>
<!-- SPHINX_SOLVER_END -->

  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace 
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>
  </NumericalMethods>
</Problem>

title: .. _ExampleDPWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Drucker-Prager Wellbore Simulation

## 1. Simulation Type and Physical Problem

This simulation models the elastoplastic behavior around a wellbore using the Drucker-Prager constitutive model with cohesion hardening. The problem represents a wellbore subjected to in-situ horizontal and vertical stresses with internal mud pressure. This is a solid mechanics problem that captures the stress redistribution and plastic deformation in the rock formation surrounding a cylindrical wellbore opening.

The configuration requires two XML files working together: a base file containing the core simulation setup and a benchmark file for validation purposes.

## 2. Required Solver Parameters and Settings

Configure a solid mechanics solver (likely named something like "SolidMechanicsLagrangianSSLE" or similar quasi-static solver) for this problem. The solver should:

- Handle elastoplastic material behavior
- Be configured for quasi-static analysis (wellbore loading problem)
- Target the computational domain containing the rock material
- Use appropriate convergence criteria for nonlinear plasticity problems
- Include sufficient load stepping to capture the elastoplastic response

## 3. Mesh Requirements

The mesh should represent a wellbore geometry with the following specifications:

- **Geometry type**: Cylindrical/annular domain representing the rock formation around the wellbore
- **Initial wellbore radius**: 0.1 meters
- **Domain extent**: Should extend sufficiently far from the wellbore to apply far-field stress boundary conditions (typically 10-20 times the wellbore radius)
- **Element type**: Appropriate for solid mechanics (hexahedral or tetrahedral elements)
- **Mesh refinement**: Higher resolution near the wellbore wall where stress concentrations and plastic deformation occur, with coarser mesh in the far-field region
- **Coordinate system**: Likely cylindrical coordinates (r, θ, z) with symmetry considerations

## 4. Material Properties and Constitutive Models

Create a material named "rock" using the **DruckerPrager** constitutive model with the following properties:

**Elastic Properties:**
- Default bulk modulus: 500 MPa (500.0e6 Pa in SI units)
- Default shear modulus: 300 MPa (300.0e6 Pa in SI units)
- Density: Must be specified (value should be appropriate for rock, units in kg/m³)

**Plasticity Parameters:**
- Default friction angle: 15.27 degrees
- Default dilation angle: 15.0 degrees
- Default cohesion: 0.1 MPa (0.1e6 Pa in SI units)
- Default hardening rate: 10.0 MPa (10.0e6 Pa in SI units)

**Hardening Law:**
- Linear hardening for cohesion is specified through the hardening rate parameter

Note: All constitutive parameters should be specified in SI units (Pa for stress/modulus quantities, degrees for angles).

## 5. Initial and Boundary Conditions

**Initial Stress State:**
- Horizontal stress (σh): -11.25 MPa (compressive, following geomechanics sign convention where negative indicates compression)
- Vertical stress (σv): -15.0 MPa (compressive)

**Boundary Conditions:**

*Far-field boundaries:*
- Apply the in-situ stress state at the outer boundaries
- Horizontal stress of -11.25 MPa acting in the horizontal plane
- Vertical stress of -15.0 MPa acting in the vertical direction

*Wellbore wall (inner boundary):*
- Apply mud pressure: -2.0 MPa (acting radially inward on the wellbore surface)
- This represents the drilling fluid pressure supporting the wellbore

*Symmetry conditions:*
- Apply appropriate symmetry boundary conditions if modeling a quarter or half section of the wellbore to reduce computational cost

## 6. Numerical Method Specifications

- **Analysis type**: Quasi-static solid mechanics
- **Material nonlinearity**: Elastoplastic behavior with hardening
- **Solution method**: Incremental loading with nonlinear iterations at each step
- **Load stepping**: The mud pressure loading should be applied incrementally to capture the evolution of the plastic zone
- **Convergence criteria**: Appropriate tolerances for force and displacement residuals in the nonlinear solver

## 7. Output Requirements

The simulation should output:

- **Field outputs**: 
  - Stress tensor components (radial, tangential, vertical, and shear stresses)
  - Displacement field
  - Plastic strain or equivalent plastic strain to visualize the plastic zone extent
  
- **Output locations**: Results along radial lines from the wellbore wall to capture the variation of stresses and displacements with distance from the wellbore

- **Validation data**: The outputs should be suitable for comparison with analytical solutions derived following the methodology from Chen and Abousleiman (2017), particularly:
  - Radial stress distribution
  - Tangential (hoop) stress distribution
  - Plastic zone radius
  - Displacement profile

- **Output format**: VTK or similar format for visualization, with time history data for key monitoring points
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_TABLE -->
  <Functions>
    <TableFunction
      name="timeFunction"
      inputVarNames="{ time }"
      coordinates="{ 0.0, 1.0, 1e99 }"
      values="{ -11.25e6, -2.0e6, -2.0e6 }"/>
  </Functions>

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_TABLE_END -->
  
  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_MATERIAL -->
  <Constitutive>
    <DruckerPrager 
      name="rock"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultBulkModulus="0.5e9"
      defaultShearModulus="0.3e9"
      defaultCohesion="0.1e6"
      defaultFrictionAngle="15.27"
      defaultDilationAngle="15.0"
      defaultHardeningRate="10.0e6"/> 

  </Constitutive>

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_MATERIAL_END -->
  <!--Assign material to geometry parts-->
  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="Omega"
      cellBlocks="{ * }"
      materialList="{ rock }"/>
  </ElementRegions>

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_BC -->
  <FieldSpecifications>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="stressXX"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="-11.25e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="stressYY"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="-11.25e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="stressZZ"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="-15.0e6"/>

    <Traction
      name="ExternalLoad"
      setNames="{ rneg }"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      scale="1.0"
      tractionType="normal"
      functionName="timeFunction"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="xconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tpos, rpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="yconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tneg, rpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="zconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ zneg, zpos }"/>
  </FieldSpecifications>

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_BC_END -->

  <Tasks>

    <!-- SPHINX_StressCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="stressCollection_rock"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/Omega/cb1"
      fieldName="rock_stress"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_StressCollectionEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollection -->
    <PackCollection
      name="displacementCollection"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollectionEnd -->

  </Tasks>

<Outputs>
    
    <!-- SPHINX_StressTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="stressHistoryOutput_rock"
      sources="{ /Tasks/stressCollection_rock }"
      filename="stressHistory_rock"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_StressTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="displacementHistoryOutput"
      sources="{ /Tasks/displacementCollection }"
      filename="displacementHistory"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementTimeHistoryEnd -->

    <VTK
      name="vtkOutput"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>  

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_SOLVER -->
  <Solvers
    gravityVector="{ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 }">
    <SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM
      name="mechanicsSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="FE1"
      targetRegions="{ Omega }"
      >
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"/>
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-5"
        newtonMaxIter="100"/>
    </SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM>
  </Solvers>

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_SOLVER_END -->
  
  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>
  </NumericalMethods>
</Problem>

title: .. _AdvancedExampleDeviatedPoroElasticWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Deviated Poro-Elastic Wellbore Injection Simulation

## Overview and Simulation Type

Create an XML configuration file for a coupled poroelastic simulation of a deviated wellbore subjected to fluid injection. This simulation models the pressure diffusion and stress redistribution in the near-wellbore region during fluid injection into an open-hole completion. The problem assumes poroelastic deformation without in-situ stresses or gravity effects. The configuration should be split into two files: a base file containing material properties and boundary conditions, and a benchmark file containing solver definitions and mesh specifications.

## Solver Configuration

### Primary Coupled Solver
Define a coupled poroelastic solver that coordinates between solid mechanics and fluid flow. This solver must:
- Be of type "Poroelastic" (or equivalent coupled hydromechanical solver)
- Reference both a solid mechanics solver and a single-phase flow solver by name
- Define a coupling strategy between the mechanical and flow components

### Solid Mechanics Solver
Configure a solid mechanics solver with the following specifications:
- Solver type: SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM (Lagrangian finite element method)
- Must be registered with a name that the poroelastic solver can reference
- Target the wellbore region mesh

### Flow Solver
Configure a single-phase flow solver with the following specifications:
- Solver type: SinglePhaseFVM (finite volume method for single-phase flow)
- Must be registered with a name that the poroelastic solver can reference
- Target the same wellbore region as the mechanics solver

## Mesh Requirements

### Mesh Generator Type
Use the internal wellbore mesh generator (InternalWellbore) to create the computational domain.

### Geometric Parameters
- **Radius specification**: Define a vector of radii that specifies the wellbore radius and the extent of the surrounding rock formation (from wellbore wall to far-field boundary)
- **Angular extent (theta)**: Specify from 0 to 180 degrees to model half the domain, taking advantage of symmetry. Note: For non-symmetric or complex scenarios, the full 360-degree domain could be specified
- **Wellbore trajectory**: Define a trajectory that creates a deviated wellbore inclined at 45 degrees in the x-z plane

### Mesh Control Parameters
- **autoSpaceRadialElems**: Set to 1 (enabled) to allow automatic optimal spacing of radial elements, with finer mesh near the wellbore transitioning to coarser mesh in the far-field
- **useCartesianOuterBoundary**: Set to 0 (disabled) for this single-region radial domain. This parameter would transform the outer boundary to a square shape if enabled

### Element Types
The mesh should generate appropriate 3D elements suitable for both the finite element solid mechanics solver and the finite volume flow solver.

## Material Properties and Constitutive Models

### Rock Mechanical Properties
Define an isotropic elastic constitutive model (ElasticIsotropic) with:
- Bulk modulus (specify the value used for the rock formation)
- Shear modulus (specify the value used for the rock formation)
- These values should be consistent with computing appropriate Poisson ratio for the analytical solution comparison

### Fluid Properties
Define a compressible single-phase fluid model (CompressibleSinglePhaseFluid) including:
- Dynamic viscosity
- Fluid compressibility

### Porosity Model
Define a Biot porosity model (BiotPorosity) containing:
- Grain bulk modulus (required for computing the Biot coefficient)
- Default/reference porosity value

### Permeability Model
Define a constant permeability model (ConstantPermeability) with:
- Uniform isotropic permeability value for the formation

## Initial Conditions

Specify initial conditions for the computational domain:
- **Initial fluid pressure**: Define the initial pore pressure throughout the domain
- **Initial porosity**: Provide the corresponding initial porosity consistent with the Biot porosity model

## Boundary Conditions

### Far-Field Boundaries
- **Mechanical**: Apply roller constraints (zero normal displacement) on the far-field boundaries
- **Flow**: Set impermeable conditions (zero flux) on the far-field boundaries

### Wellbore Wall Boundary
- **Location**: Apply to the nodeset named "rneg" which is automatically generated by the internal wellbore mesh generator for the wellbore face
- **Pressure loading**: Define a face pressure field specification
- **Injection pressure**: The scale value should be negative to denote fluid injection (pressure applied into the formation)
- **Pressure value**: Set to p0 (the characteristic injection pressure used in the analytical solution, value needed for comparison)

### Symmetry Boundaries
Apply appropriate symmetry conditions on the planes of symmetry (at theta = 0 and theta = 180 degrees)

## Numerical Method Specifications

The simulation requires:
- Coupled hydromechanical formulation based on poroelasticity theory
- Lagrangian finite element discretization for solid mechanics
- Finite volume discretization for single-phase flow
- Time-stepping scheme capable of capturing the transient diffusion process
- Simulation should run for at least 78 seconds to capture the pressure diffusion results shown in validation

## Output Requirements

Configure outputs to capture:
- Fluid pressure distribution in the near-wellbore region (for visualization and validation against analytical solutions)
- Radial stress distribution along the radial direction from wellbore
- Hoop stress distribution for comparison with analytical expressions
- Results should be extractable for comparison with the Detournay and Cheng (1988) analytical solutions involving:
  - Pore pressure as a function of dimensionless radius and time
  - Radial stress incorporating Biot coefficient and Poisson ratio effects
  - Hoop stress computed from pressure and radial stress

## File Organization

The configuration should be organized into two XML files:
1. **Base file** (DeviatedPoroElasticWellbore_Injection_base.xml): Contains material/constitutive definitions and boundary condition specifications
2. **Benchmark file** (DeviatedPoroElasticWellbore_Injection_benchmark.xml): Contains solver definitions and mesh specifications, with includes/references to the base file
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  
  <Events
    maxTime="78.0">
    <!-- SPHINX_Execution -->
    <PeriodicEvent
      name="solverApplications"
      forceDt="0.78"
      target="/Solvers/poroSolve"/>

    <!-- SPHINX_ExecutionEnd -->
    <PeriodicEvent
      name="outputs"
      timeFrequency="7.8"
      target="/Outputs/siloOutput"/>

    <PeriodicEvent
      name="restarts"
      timeFrequency="39"
      targetExactTimestep="0"
      target="/Outputs/restartOutput"/>
  </Events>

  <!-- SPHINX_FEDiscretization -->
  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>

    <FiniteVolume>
      <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="singlePhaseTPFA"/>
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <!-- SPHINX_FEDiscretizationEnd -->
  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="Omega"
      cellBlocks="{ * }"
      materialList="{ water, porousRock }"/>
  </ElementRegions>

  <Constitutive>
    <!-- SPHINX_Material -->
    <PorousElasticIsotropic
      name="porousRock"
      solidModelName="rock"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"/>

    <ElasticIsotropic
      name="rock"
      defaultDensity="0"
      defaultBulkModulus="11039657020.4"
      defaultShearModulus="8662741799.83"/>

    <!--  BiotCoefficient="0.771"
          BiotModulus=15.8e9 -->
    <CompressibleSinglePhaseFluid
      name="water"

    <ConstantPermeability

title: .. _AdvancedExamplePureThermalDiffusionWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Pure Thermal Diffusion Around a Wellbore Simulation

## 1. Simulation Type and Physical Problem

This simulation models pure thermal diffusion around a wellbore using GEOS's thermal single-phase flow solver. The problem represents a validation study comparing numerical results against the analytical solution from Wang and Papamichos (1994).

The physical scenario involves:
- A wellbore with a uniform temperature applied on its inner curved surface
- Temperature diffusing radially outward into the surrounding rock medium
- Pure thermal diffusion only (no thermal convection or fluid flow)
- To achieve pure thermal diffusion behavior, fluid pressure must be set to zero everywhere and fluid heat capacity must be set to a negligible value

The analytical solution being validated is: T(r) = T_in × sqrt(R_in/r) × erfc((r - R_in)/(2×sqrt(c_T×t))), where r is the radial coordinate, T_in is the wellbore surface temperature, R_in is the wellbore inner radius, c_T is the thermal diffusion coefficient (thermal conductivity divided by volumetric heat capacity), and t is time.

## 2. Required Solver Parameters and Settings

Configure a thermal single-phase flow solver with the following characteristics:
- Solver type: SinglePhaseFVM (or equivalent thermal single-phase flow solver)
- The solver must be capable of handling thermal transport
- Enable the thermal option for single-phase flow
- The problem is inherently transient (time-dependent diffusion)
- Time stepping should be configured to capture the diffusion evolution

## 3. Mesh Requirements

The mesh should represent a 2D wellbore geometry:
- Two-dimensional domain (radial cross-section around wellbore)
- The geometry must include a wellbore inner surface at radius R_in
- Extend radially outward to a far-field boundary
- Use appropriate element types for 2D analysis (likely quadrilateral or triangular elements)
- The mesh should be refined near the wellbore surface where temperature gradients are steepest
- The mesh must have named sets/regions for:
  - The wellbore inner curved surface (for applying temperature boundary condition)
  - The far-field boundary (for applying far-field temperature)
  - The entire domain (for initial conditions)

## 4. Material Properties and Constitutive Models

### Solid Internal Energy Model
Create a SolidInternalEnergy constitutive model to define the volumetric heat capacity of the rock medium around the wellbore. This should be a linear model specifying:
- Volumetric heat capacity of the solid matrix
- Reference temperature for the energy calculation

### Thermal Conductivity Model
Create a SinglePhaseConstantThermalConductivity constitutive model to define the thermal conductivity of the medium. This requires:
- A constant thermal conductivity value for the rock
- The thermal diffusion coefficient c_T is derived from: c_T = thermal conductivity / volumetric heat capacity

### Fluid Model
Create a ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid constitutive model with:
- Volumetric heat capacity set to a negligible (near-zero) value to exclude thermal convection effects
- Standard fluid properties (density, viscosity, compressibility) though these will have minimal effect since pressure is zero
- Thermal expansion coefficient (can be set to nominal value)

## 5. Initial and Boundary Conditions

### Temperature Field Specifications
All temperature conditions are applied as Dirichlet face boundary conditions using the faceManager:

**Initial Temperature:**
- Apply an initial temperature field to the entire domain
- This sets the starting temperature distribution before the wellbore heating begins

**Wellbore Surface Temperature (T_in):**
- Apply a fixed/imposed temperature on the curved inner wellbore surface
- This represents the heat source driving the diffusion
- Use appropriate face set name corresponding to the wellbore inner surface

**Far-Field Temperature:**
- Apply a fixed temperature at the far-field boundary
- This maintains the original formation temperature at distance from the wellbore

### Pressure Field Specifications
Although this is a pure thermal diffusion problem, GEOS requires pressure specifications since thermal transfer is coupled with fluid flow:

**Fluid Pressure:**
- Set fluid pressure to zero everywhere in the domain
- Apply as both initial condition and boundary conditions
- This effectively eliminates fluid flow and convective heat transfer
- Use faceManager to apply pressure boundary conditions

## 6. Numerical Method Specifications

- Finite volume method (FVM) discretization for thermal transport
- The solver handles the diffusion equation implicitly
- Time integration should use appropriate time steps to resolve the thermal diffusion timescale
- The characteristic diffusion time scale relates to: t ~ L²/c_T, where L is a characteristic length
- Nonlinear solver tolerances should be set appropriately for convergence
- Linear solver settings for the coupled thermal-flow system

## 7. Output Requirements

Configure outputs to:
- Record temperature field at multiple time steps for comparison with analytical solution
- Output temperature profiles along the radial direction from wellbore surface outward
- Enable visualization of the 2D temperature distribution
- Store results at time intervals that capture the diffusion front evolution
- Include nodal or cell-centered temperature values
- Output format should support plotting temperature vs. radial distance for validation against the analytical Wang and Papamichos (1994) solution

The validation comparison should show good agreement between GEOS numerical results and the analytical solution for radial temperature distribution at various times.
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <Solvers>
    <SinglePhaseFVM
      name="singleFlow"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="tpfaFlow"
      temperature="0"
      isThermal="1"
      targetRegions="{ region }">
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-6"
        newtonMaxIter="100"/>
      <LinearSolverParameters
        directParallel="0"/>
    </SinglePhaseFVM>
  </Solvers>

  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteVolume>
      <TwoPointFluxApproximation
        name="tpfaFlow"/>
    </FiniteVolume>
  </NumericalMethods>

  <Constitutive>

    <CompressibleSolidConstantPermeability
      name="rock_linear"
      solidModelName="nullSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy_linear"/>

    <CompressibleSolidConstantPermeability
      name="rock_temperatureDependentVolumetricHeatCapacity"
      solidModelName="nullSolid"
      porosityModelName="rockPorosity"
      permeabilityModelName="rockPerm"
      solidInternalEnergyModelName="rockInternalEnergy_nonLinear"/>

    <NullModel
      name="nullSolid"/>

    <PressurePorosity
      name="rockPorosity"
      defaultReferencePorosity="0.1"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      compressibility="3.0e-11"/>

	<!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_linear -->
    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="rockInternalEnergy_linear"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="1.0e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_linearEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_nonLinear -->
    <SolidInternalEnergy
      name="rockInternalEnergy_nonLinear"
      referenceVolumetricHeatCapacity="4.56e6"
      dVolumetricHeatCapacity_dTemperature="1e6"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SolidInternalEnergy_nonLinearEnd -->

    <ConstantPermeability
      name="rockPerm"
      permeabilityComponents="{ 1.0e-18, 1.0e-18, 1.0e-18 }"/>

	<!-- SPHINX_ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid -->
    <ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluid
      name="fluid"
      defaultDensity="1000"
      defaultViscosity="0.001"
      referencePressure="0.0"
      referenceTemperature="0"
      compressibility="5e-10"
      thermalExpansionCoeff="3e-4"
      viscosibility="0.0"
      specificHeatCapacity="1"
      referenceInternalEnergy="0.99"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_ThermalCompressibleSinglePhaseFluidEnd -->

    <!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_linear -->
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="thermalCond_linear"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.66, 1.66, 1.66 }"
      thermalConductivityGradientComponents="{ 0, 0, 0 }"
      referenceTemperature="0"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_linearEnd -->    

	<!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_nonLinear -->
    <SinglePhaseThermalConductivity
      name="thermalCond_nonLinear"
      defaultThermalConductivityComponents="{ 1.5, 1.5, 1.5 }"
      thermalConductivityGradientComponents="{ -12e-4, -12e-4, -12e-4 }"
      referenceTemperature="20"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_SinglePhaseThermalConductivity_nonLinearEnd -->    
	
  </Constitutive>

  <FieldSpecifications>

	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedPressure -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialPressure"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/region/cb"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkPressure"
      setNames="{ rpos }"       
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sourcePressure"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="pressure"
      scale="0e6"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedPressureEnd -->

	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedTemperature -->
    <FieldSpecification
      name="initialTemperature"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions/region/cb"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sinkTemperature"
      setNames="{ rpos }"       
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="100"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="sourceTemperature"
      setNames="{ rneg }"     
      objectPath="faceManager"
      fieldName="temperature"
      scale="-20.0"/>
	<!-- SPHINX_FieldSpecificationImposedTemperatureEnd -->

  </FieldSpecifications>

  <Outputs>
    <VTK
      name="vtkOutput"/>

    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>
</Problem>

title: .. _ExampleMCCWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Modified Cam-Clay Wellbore Problem XML Configuration

## 1. Simulation Type and Physical Problem

This simulation models a drained vertical wellbore problem with elastoplastic deformation using the Modified Cam-Clay constitutive model. The physical scenario involves a wellbore subjected to isotropic horizontal stress and vertical stress, where increasing the wellbore supporting pressure causes the wellbore to expand. This expansion induces elastoplastic deformation in the surrounding formation rock, developing a plastic zone in the near-wellbore region. The simulation is quasi-static, meaning inertial effects are neglected. This is a solid mechanics problem without pore pressure variation (drained conditions).

## 2. Solver Parameters and Settings

Create a solid mechanics solver with the following specifications:
- Solver name: "mechanicsSolver"
- Solver type: SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM (Lagrangian finite element formulation)
- Problem type: QuasiStatic (no inertial effects)
- Discretization method: Reference a finite element discretization named "FE1"
- Material association: Reference a material named "rock"
- Target regions: The computational domain cell block "cb1"

## 3. Mesh Requirements

Use the internal wellbore mesh generator (InternalWellbore) with the following specifications:

**Domain Dimensions:**
- Overall domain size: 10 meters × 5 meters × 2 meters
- Initial wellbore radius: 0.1 meters

**Wellbore Trajectory:**
- Define a vertical well trajectory using coordinate points

**Element Configuration:**
- Element counts: 50 elements in radial direction, 40 elements in tangential direction, 2 elements in z-direction
- Element type: Eight-node hexahedral elements (C3D8)
- Enable automatic spacing for radial elements by setting autoSpaceRadialElems to 1 (this overrides manual nr values)
- Set useCartesianOuterBoundary to 0 to enforce a Cartesian-aligned outer boundary on the outer block

**Cell Block:**
- Name the mesh cell block "cb1"
- Mesh refinement should conform to the wellbore geometry

## 4. Material Properties and Constitutive Models

Define a single homogeneous material using the Modified Cam-Clay (ModifiedCamClay) constitutive model with the following parameters:

- Material name: "rock"
- Reference Pressure (Pr): 120 kPa
- Shear Modulus (G): 4302 kPa
- PreConsolidation Pressure (Pc): 169 kPa
- Slope of Critical State Line (M): 1.2
- Virgin Compression Index (cc): 0.072676
- Recompression Index (cr): 0.014535
- Density: Specify appropriate value in SI units (kg/m³)

Note: All constitutive parameters should be specified in the International System of Units.

## 5. Initial and Boundary Conditions

### Initial Conditions (all must have initialCondition field set to 1):

**In-situ Stress State:**
- Horizontal stress (σh): -100 kPa (applied in both x and y directions as initial stress components)
- Vertical stress (σv): -160 kPa (applied in z direction as initial stress component)

**Initial Wellbore Traction:**
- Apply initial compressive traction at the wellbore wall (face set "rneg"): -100 kPa at time t = 0 seconds

### Boundary Conditions:

**Wellbore Wall Loading (face set "rneg"):**
- Traction type: normal (pressure applied as product of scale and outward face normal)
- Scale value: -1.0e5 (representing -100 kPa base value)
- Time-dependent loading: Use a table function named "timeFunction" to define the external load
- The traction increases from -100 kPa to -300 kPa following a linear time history

**Table Function for Time-Dependent Loading:**
- Create a function named "timeFunction"
- Define coordinates (time values) and corresponding values (magnitude multipliers)
- The loading magnitude should increase linearly as time evolves
- Final mud pressure: -300 kPa

**Roller Constraints on Outer Boundaries:**
- Apply displacement constraints on the following boundary faces:
  - xneg face: Constrain displacement in x-direction (component 0) to zero
  - xpos face: Constrain displacement in x-direction (component 0) to zero
  - ypos face: Constrain displacement in y-direction (component 1) to zero
  - yneg face: Constrain displacement in y-direction (component 1) to zero
  - zpos face: Constrain displacement in z-direction (component 2) to zero
  - zneg face: Constrain displacement in z-direction (component 2) to zero

**Object Path Specifications:**
- Use "nodeManager" in objectPath for displacement constraints (applied to element nodes)
- Use "faceManager" in objectPath for traction boundary conditions (applied to element faces)

## 6. Numerical Method Specifications

Define a numerical methods section that includes:
- A finite element discretization named "FE1"
- This discretization should be compatible with the SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM solver
- Appropriate for eight-node hexahedral (C3D8) elements

## 7. Output Requirements

Configure output in silo format for visualization in VisIt:
- Output stress field data, particularly the tangential stress component (σθθ)
- Output displacement field data
- Enable output of results for the near-wellbore region
- Output should support comparison with analytical solutions for:
  - Normal stress component distributions
  - Stress path
  - Supporting wellbore pressure
  - Wellbore size

## Additional Notes

- The simulation requires two XML files: a base file containing solver, material, boundary conditions, and table function definitions, and a benchmark file containing the mesh definition
- Use include/import mechanism to combine the base and benchmark files
- Sign convention: Compressive stresses are negative in GEOS
- The setName field in field specifications should reference predefined geometric sets (rneg for wellbore wall, xneg, xpos, ypos, yneg, zpos, zneg for outer boundaries)
- fieldName must match registered field names in GEOS (e.g., for stress components and displacement)
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_TABLE -->
  <Functions>
    <TableFunction
      name="timeFunction"
      inputVarNames="{ time }"
      coordinates="{ 0.0, 1.0 }"
      values="{ 1.0, 3.0 }"/>
  </Functions>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_TABLE_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_MATERIAL -->
  <Constitutive>
    <ModifiedCamClay
      name="rock"
      defaultDensity="2700"
      defaultRefPressure="-1.2e5"
      defaultRefStrainVol="-0.0"
      defaultShearModulus="4.302e6"
      defaultPreConsolidationPressure="-1.69e5"
      defaultCslSlope="1.2"
      defaultVirginCompressionIndex="0.072676"
      defaultRecompressionIndex="0.014535"      
    />
  </Constitutive>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_MATERIAL_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_ELEMENTREGIONS -->
  <ElementRegions>
    <CellElementRegion
      name="Omega"
      cellBlocks="{ * }"
      materialList="{ rock }"/>
  </ElementRegions>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_ELEMENTREGIONS_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_BC -->
  <FieldSpecifications>
    <FieldSpecification
      name="stressXX"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="0"
      scale="-1.0e5"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="stressYY"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="1"
      scale="-1.0e5"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="stressZZ"
      initialCondition="1"
      setNames="{ all }"
      objectPath="ElementRegions"
      fieldName="rock_stress"
      component="2"
      scale="-1.6e5"/>

    <Traction
      name="ExternalLoad"
      setNames="{ rneg }"
      objectPath="faceManager"
      scale="-1.0e5"
      tractionType="normal"
      functionName="timeFunction"/> 

    <FieldSpecification
      name="xconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="0"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ xneg, xpos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="yconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="1"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ tneg, tpos, ypos }"/>

    <FieldSpecification
      name="zconstraint"
      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"
      component="2"
      scale="0.0"
      setNames="{ zneg, zpos }"/>   
  </FieldSpecifications>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_BC_END --> 

  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_OUTPUT -->
  <Outputs>
    <Silo 
      name="siloOutput"
      parallelThreads="1"
      plotFileRoot="plot"
    />
    <Restart
      name="restartOutput"/>
  </Outputs>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_OUTPUT_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_SOLVER -->
  <Solvers
    gravityVector="{ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 }">
    <SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM
      name="mechanicsSolver"
      logLevel="1"
      discretization="FE1"
      targetRegions="{ Omega }"
      >
      <LinearSolverParameters
      directParallel="0"/>
      <NonlinearSolverParameters
        newtonTol="1.0e-5"
        newtonMaxIter="15"/>
    </SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM>
  </Solvers>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_SOLVER_END -->

  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_NUMERICAL -->
  <NumericalMethods>
    <FiniteElements>
      <FiniteElementSpace
        name="FE1"
        order="1"/>
    </FiniteElements>
  </NumericalMethods>
  <!-- SPHINX_WELLBORE_NUMERICAL_END -->
  
</Problem>

title: .. _ExampleEDPWellbore:
natural_language_spec:
# Natural Language Specification for Extended Drucker-Prager Wellbore Simulation

## Overview and Simulation Type

Create an XML configuration file for a three-dimensional drained wellbore elastoplastic deformation simulation using GEOS. This simulation models the contraction of a vertical wellbore subjected to in-situ stresses when the wellbore supporting pressure is reduced. The analysis uses the Extended Drucker-Prager constitutive model to capture elastoplastic behavior in the near-wellbore region. The simulation is quasi-static, meaning inertial effects are not considered.

The configuration is split across two XML files: a base file containing solver, material, boundary conditions, and function definitions, and a benchmark file containing the mesh specification.

---

## Solver Configuration

Define a solid mechanics solver using the Lagrangian finite element formulation with the following specifications:

- **Solver type**: SolidMechanicsLagrangianFEM
- **Solver name**: mechanicsSolver
- **Problem type**: QuasiStatic (no inertial effects)
- **Discretization method**: Reference a finite element discretization named "FE1" defined in the NumericalMethods section
- **Material association**: The solver should reference a material named "rock"
- **Target region**: The solver should operate on the cell block region created by the mesh

---

## Numerical Methods

Define a finite element discretization in the NumericalMethods section:

- **Discretization name**: FE1
- This discretization will be used by the solid mechanics solver for spatial discretization of the governing equations

---

## Mesh Requirements

Use the internal wellbore mesh generator to create a structured three-dimensional mesh:

- **Mesh generator type**: InternalWellbore
- **Domain dimensions**: 10 meters × 10 meters × 2 meters (representing the rock domain around the wellbore)
- **Wellbore radius**: 0.1 meters (initial radius)
- **Wellbore trajectory**: Define coordinates that represent a vertical well
- **Radial element spacing**: Enable automatic spacing of radial elements using the autoSpaceRadialElems parameter set to 1, which will override manual nr (number of radial elements) values
- **Element type**: Eight-node hexahedral elements (C3D8)
- **Cell block name**: cb1
- **Mesh refinement**: The mesh should be refined to conform with the wellbore geometry, with finer elements near the wellbore wall and coarser elements toward the far field

---

## Constitutive Model and Material Properties

Define material properties in the Constitutive section using the Extended Drucker-Prager elastoplastic model:

- **Constitutive model type**: ExtendedDruckerPrager
- **Material name**: rock

**Elastic properties:**
- Bulk modulus (K): 500 MPa
- Shear modulus (G): 300 MPa

**Plastic properties (Mohr-Coulomb failure envelope parameters):**
- Cohesion (defaultCohesion): 0.0 MPa (zero cohesion to match analytical reference)
- Initial friction angle (defaultInitialFrictionAngle): 15.27 degrees
- Residual friction angle (defaultResidualFrictionAngle): 23.05 degrees
- Hardening rate (defaultHardening): 0.01 (dimensionless)
- Dilation ratio (defaultDilationRatio): 1.0 (this corresponds to an associated plastic flow rule)

**Additional properties:**
- Density: Specify in SI units (the exact value should be defined based on typical rock properties)

Note: Since the residual friction angle (23.05°) is larger than the initial friction angle (15.27°), this defines a strain hardening model.

---

## Initial Conditions

All initial condition fields must have the initialCondition attribute set to 1 (true).

**In-situ stress state:**
- Isotropic horizontal stress (σh): -11.25 MPa (negative indicates compression per GEOS sign convention)
- Vertical stress (σv): -15.0 MPa (negative indicates compression)

**Initial wellbore wall traction:**
- Apply an initial compressive traction of -11.25 MPa at the wellbore wall (surface named "rneg") at time t = 0 seconds to establish equilibrium with the in-situ horizontal stress

---

## Boundary Conditions

Define boundary conditions in the FieldSpecifications section:

**Wellbore wall loading (surface "rneg"):**
- Apply traction with tractionType set to "normal"
- Use scale value of 1.0
- The traction is applied as a pressure specified from the product of scale and the outward face normal
- Reference a time-dependent table function named "timeFunction" to control the loading magnitude
- The wellbore pressure starts at -11.25 MPa and is linearly reduced to -2.0 MPa over the simulation time

**Roller constraints:**
- Apply roller constraints on boundaries "tneg" and "tpos"

**Plane strain conditions:**
- Fix vertical displacement (component 2, z-direction) on surfaces "zneg" and "zpos" to enforce plane strain conditions

**Far-field boundary:**
- Fix horizontal displacement on the far-field boundary to prevent rigid body motion

**Object path specifications:**
- Use "nodeManager" in objectPath for displacement boundary conditions applied to element nodes
- Use "faceManager" in objectPath for traction boundary conditions applied to element faces

**Component conventions:**
- Component 0 = x-direction
- Component 1 = y-direction  
- Component 2 = z-direction

---

## Table Function for Time-Dependent Loading

Define a table function in the Functions section:

- **Function name**: timeFunction
- **Function type**: TableFunction
- **Purpose**: Define the time-dependent wellbore traction for the "ExternalLoad" boundary condition
- **Coordinates**: Define time values as the independent variable
- **Values**: Define corresponding traction magnitudes
- **Loading history**: The loading magnitude should decrease linearly from the initial value (-11.25 MPa) to the final value (-2.0 MPa) as time progresses

The coordinates and values together form time-magnitude pairs that describe the complete loading time history.

---

## Output Requirements

Configure output to generate HDF5 format files for post-processing:

- Enable HDF5 output for visualization and comparison with analytical solutions
- Output should include displacement fields and stress fields around the wellbore
- Results will be used to validate against analytical solutions from Chen and Abousleiman (2017)

The output data should capture:
- Principal stress component distributions
- Stress path on the wellbore surface
- Supporting wellbore pressure evolution
- Wellbore size/deformation

---

## Additional Notes

- All stress values use negative sign convention for compression (standard GEOS convention)
- The shorthand location identifiers used for boundary condition application include:
  - "rneg": wellbore wall (inner radius)
  - "tneg" and "tpos": boundaries for roller constraints
  - "zneg" and "zpos": top and bottom surfaces for plane strain
  - "xpos", "ypos": far-field boundaries
- The setName field in boundary conditions should reference the appropriate geometric regions defined by the mesh generator
- The fieldName attribute should reference registered GEOS field names for displacement and stress components
xml_content:
<?xml version="1.0" ?>

<Problem>
  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_TABLE -->
  <Functions>
    <TableFunction
      name="timeFunction"
      inputVarNames="{ time }"
      coordinates="{ 0.0, 1.0, 1e99 }"

  <Constitutive>

    <FieldSpecification

      component="2"

    <Traction
      name="ExternalLoad"
      setNames="{ rneg }"

      tractionType="normal"

    <FieldSpecification
      name="xconstraint"

    <FieldSpecification

      component="2"

  <!-- SPHINX_DP_WELLBORE_BC_END -->

  <Tasks>

    <!-- SPHINX_StressCollection -->

    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollection -->
    <PackCollection

      objectPath="nodeManager"
      fieldName="totalDisplacement"/>
    <!-- SPHINX_DisplacementCollectionEnd -->

  </Tasks>

<Outputs>
    
    <!-- SPHINX_StressTimeHistory -->
    <TimeHistory
      name="stressHistoryOutput_rock"
      sources="{ /Tasks/stressCollection_rock }"

    <!-- SPHINX_StressTimeHistoryEnd -->
